{{Short description|Colombian politician (1989–2026)}} {{Use dmy dates|date=August 2025}} {{Infobox officeholder | honorific_prefix = | name = Diógenes Quintero | honorific_suffix = | image = File:Diógenes Quintero.jpg | caption = | office = Member of the [[Chamber of Representatives of Colombia|Chamber of Representatives]] | constituency = Special Transitory Peace Constituency of Catatumbo, [[Norte de Santander]] | term_start = 13 March 2022 | term_end = 28 January 2026 | birth_name = Diógenes Quintero Amaya | birth_date = {{birth date|1989|05|29|df=y}} | birth_place = [[Hacarí]], Norte de Santander, Colombia | death_date = {{death date and age|2026|01|28|1989|05|29|df=y}} | death_place = [[La Playa de Belén]], Norte de Santander, Colombia | party = ASODES (Association of Displaced Families of Hacarí)
[[Union Party for the People]] | other_party = | education = [[Free University of Colombia]]
[[Universidad Externado de Colombia]] | website = }} '''Diógenes Quintero Amaya'''{{efn|{{ipa|es|diˈoxenes kinˈteɾo aˈmaʝa}}. {{Family name explanation|[[Quintero (surname)|Quintero]]|[[Amaya (surname)|Amaya]]|lang=Hispanic American}}}} (29 May 1989 – 28 January 2026) was a Colombian lawyer, human rights defender and politician. He served in the [[Chamber of Representatives of Colombia|Chamber of Representatives]] for the Special Transitory Peace Constituency of Catatumbo between 2022 and 2026, where he became one of the most representative figures of the peace seats created after the [[Colombian peace process|Peace Agreement]]. He was killed in [[SATENA Flight 8849|a plane crash]] in [[Norte de Santander]] while campaigning for re-election to Congress. ==Early life and education== Quintero was born on 29 May 1989 in the village of Agua Blanca, in the municipality of [[Hacarí]], in the [[Catatumbo region]] of Norte de Santander, an area historically affected by the [[Colombian conflict|armed conflict]], forced displacement, and the absence of the state.{{cite web |url=https://www.elespectador.com/politica/diogenes-quintero-velar-por-el-catatumbo-desde-el-congreso/ |title=Diógenes Quintero: velar por el Catatumbo desde el Congreso |date=1 June 2023 |author=Daniela Cristancho |access-date=28 January 2026 |website=[[El Espectador]]}} His father was president of the local community action board for more than three decades, which influenced his early interest in social leadership and community participation. He studied law at the [[Free University of Colombia]], Cúcuta campus. He later obtained a specialization in administrative law and pursued a master's degree in management for development at the [[Universidad Externado de Colombia]].{{cite web |url=https://www.lasillavacia.com/quien-es-quien/quien-es-diogenes-quintero-amaya/ |title=Quién es Diógenes Quintero Amaya |date=22 March 2024 |access-date=28 January 2026 |website=La Silla Vacía|language=es}} ==Professional career== Quintero began his public career as a contractor for the [[Ombudsman's Office of Colombia|Ombudsman's Office]]. Later, he served as the municipal ombudsman of Hacarí, a position from which he supported victims of the armed conflict and denounced human rights violations. During this period, he was the victim of threats and an attack on his home, which forced him to resign. In 2019, Quintero was appointed regional ombudsman in [[Ocaña, Colombia|Ocaña]], one of the areas with the highest rates of violence in Norte de Santander.{{cite web |url=https://caracol.com.co/emisora/2022/03/15/cucuta/1647357721_711587.html |title="Trabajaré por el Catatumbo": Diógenes Quintero, curul de paz |date=15 March 2022 |access-date=28 January 2026 |website=[[Caracol Radio]]|language=es}} He founded and served as president of the Association of Ombudsmen of Catatumbo, an organization focused on the defense of human rights and institutional strengthening in the region.{{cite web|url=https://www.camara.gov.co/representantes/diogenes-quintero-amaya|title=Diógenes Quintero Amaya|date=9 May 2025 |publisher=Chamber of Representatives of Colombia|access-date=29 January 2026|language=es}} ==Political career== ===Chamber of Representatives=== In the [[2022 Colombian parliamentary election|2022 legislative elections]], Quintero was elected to the Chamber of Representatives for the Special Transitory Peace Constituency of Catatumbo,{{efn|Comprising the municipalities of [[Convención]], [[El Carmen, Norte de Santander|El Carmen]], [[El Tarra]], [[Hacarí]], [[San Calixto]], [[Sardinata]], [[Teorama]] and [[Tibú]].}} one of the 16 special seats created within the framework of the Peace Agreement for the regions most affected by the armed conflict.{{cite web |url=https://www.eltiempo.com/elecciones-2022/congreso/curules-de-paz-estos-son-los-representantes-electos-658393 |title=Curules para la paz: Estas son las 16 personas que van a llegar a ocuparlas |date=15 March 2022 |access-date=28 January 2026 |website=[[El Tiempo (Colombia)|El Tiempo]]|language=es}} He obtained approximately 5,700 votes and was endorsed by organizations of victims of forced displacement. During his legislative term, Quintero was a member of, among others, the First Permanent Constitutional Commission, the Third Permanent Constitutional Commission, and the Interparliamentary Commission on Public Credit.{{cite web |url=https://www.camara.gov.co/diogenes-quintero-amaya-nuevo-integrante-de-la-comision-interparlamentaria-de-credito-publico/ |title=Diógenes Quintero Amaya, nuevo integrante de la Comisión Interparlamentaria de Crédito Público |date=25 February 2025 |access-date=28 January 2026 |website=[[Chamber of Representatives of Colombia]]|language=es}} His work focused on the implementation of the Peace Agreement, comprehensive rural reform, victims' rights, and strengthening rural development in the Catatumbo region.{{cite web |url=https://www.eluniverso.com/noticias/internacional/el-congresista-colombiano-diogenes-quintero-iba-entre-los-pasajeros-de-avion-desaparecido-en-noreste-del-pais-nota/ |title=El congresista colombiano Diógenes Quintero iba entre los pasajeros de avión desaparecido en noreste del país |date=28 January 2026|access-date=28 January 2026 |website=[[El Universo]]}} ===Controversy=== Quintero's election was challenged by Ascamcat, a campesino association based in Catatumbo, which alleged that he was ineligible to serve, that there had been irregularities in the vote count, and that the mayor of Hacarí had shown favouritism towards his candidacy. The [[Council of State (Colombia)|Council of State]], however, dismissed the claims and upheld his election to the Chamber. ===Re-election=== On 5 December 2025, Quintero registered to seek re-election in the [[2026 Colombian parliamentary election|March 2026 legislative election]].{{cite news |last1=Suárez |first1=Astrid |title=Cause of plane crash in Colombia that killed 15, including Congress member, under investigation |url=https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/cause-plane-crash-colombia-killed-15-including-congress-129685219 |agency=ABC News |date=29 January 2026}} ==Death and legacy== {{main|SATENA Flight 8849}} On 28 January 2026, Quintero died in a plane crash in the rural area of the municipality of [[La Playa de Belén]], Norte de Santander, while traveling on a regional flight operated by the airline [[SATENA]] from [[Cúcuta]] to Ocaña; his assistant, Natalia Acosta, and other members of his team were also on the flight.{{cite web |url=https://www.noticiasrcn.com/colombia/quien-era-diogenes-quintero-el-congresista-que-murio-en-la-avioneta-de-satena-985554 |title=¿Quién era Diógenes Quintero, el congresista que murió en la avioneta de Satena? |date=28 January 2026 |access-date=28 January 2026 |website=Noticias RCN|language=es}}{{cite web |url=https://www.infobae.com/colombia/2026/01/28/luto-en-el-capitolio-por-muerte-del-representante-diogenes-quintero-estos-son-los-congresistas-fallecidos-en-el-presente-cuatrienio/ |title=Luto en el Capitolio por muerte del representante Diógenes Quintero: estos son los congresistas fallecidos en el presente cuatrienio |date=28 January 2026 |author=Mario Alejandro Rodríguez |access-date=28 January 2026 |website=[[Infobae]]|language=es}} He is remembered as one of the leading voices of the Catatumbo region in the Congress of the Republic and as a representative of the communities victimized by the armed conflict, standing out for his commitment to peace, human rights, and rural development. ==Notes== {{notelist}} ==References== {{reflist}} {{Authority control}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Quintero, Diogenes}} [[Category:1989 births]] [[Category:2026 deaths]] [[Category:People from Norte de Santander Department]] [[Category:Members of the Chamber of Representatives of Colombia]] [[Category:Colombian human rights activists]] [[Category:21st-century Colombian lawyers]] [[Category:Free University of Colombia alumni]] [[Category:Universidad Externado de Colombia alumni]] [[Category:Victims of aviation accidents or incidents in Colombia]] [[Category:Victims of aviation accidents or incidents in 2026]] [[Category:21st-century Colombian politicians]]

{{nihongo|'''Takato Ishida'''|石田 嵩人|Ishida Takato|born 5 February 1990|lead=yes}} is a Japanese politician who has been the governor of [[Fukui Prefecture]] since 2026. He was previously a diplomat under the [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Japan)|Ministry of Foreign Affairs]] in [[Zambia]] and Australia. He resigned his ministry post to run for governor after his predecessor’s resignation and won the January 2026 election, campaigning on child‑rearing support, crisis management and greater use of social media to engage voters.

== Early life and education ==
Ishida was born on 5 February 1990 in [[Fukui (city)|Fukui]], [[Fukui Prefecture]], Japan.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pref.fukui.lg.jp/doc/senkan/r8tijikengihosen/r8tijikengihosen_d/fil/senkyokouhou.pdf|title=令和8年1月25日執行 福井県知事選挙候補者選挙公報|website=pref.fukui.lg.jp|language=ja|access-date=20 March 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260111144329/https://www.pref.fukui.lg.jp/doc/senkan/r8tijikengihosen/r8tijikengihosen_d/fil/senkyokouhou.pdf|archive-date=11 January 2026}}</ref> His father was a surgeon, and Ishida lived in [[London]], England, because of his father's work while he was in the sixth grade.<ref>{{cite web |title=石田 嵩人氏｜同窓生のご紹介 |url=https://www.kansaigaidai-dousou.jp/alumnus/index.php?c=introduction_view&pk=1754528806 |access-date=1 October 2026 |website=関西外国語大学・短期大学部同窓会 |publisher=[[Kansai Gaidai University]] |language=ja}}</ref> Ishida later recalled that news coverage in Britain of the [[September 11 attacks]] in 2001 led him to become interested in international relations.<ref>{{cite web |title=石田 嵩人氏｜同窓生のご紹介 |url=https://www.kansaigaidai-dousou.jp/alumnus/index.php?c=introduction_view&pk=1754528806 |access-date=1 October 2026 |website=関西外国語大学・短期大学部同窓会 |publisher=[[Kansai Gaidai University]] |language=ja}}</ref>  

In 2012, Ishida graduated from [[Kansai Gaidai University]] and [[Pacific University]] with dual bachelor's degrees in communications and [[international relations]], respectively. As an undergraduate, he entered a study abroad program intended to prepare students for careers in international organizations such as the [[United Nations]], which allowed him to study in the U.S. in [[Oregon]].<ref name=":0">{{cite web|url=https://www.kansaigaidai.ac.jp/magazine/job-hunting-job-introduction/990/|title=現役外交官によるキャリアトーク第1回「Diplomacy（外交）という仕事 ～人生を変えた海外挑戦～」|language=ja|website=Kansai Gaidai Web Magazine}}</ref> He then obtained a [[Master of Science in Foreign Service]] from [[Georgetown University]] in 2018 and began studying for a doctorate in [[security studies]] from the [[National Graduate Institute for Policy Studies]] in 2022.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.matichon.co.th/foreign/news_5568419|title=ทาคาโตะ อิชิดะ อดีตนักการทูตวัย 35 ชนะเลือกตั้ง นั่ง ผู้ว่าฯจ.ฟุกุอิ ที่ อายุน้อยที่สุดในญี่ปุ่น|language=th|date=27 January 2026|website=[[Matichon]]}}</ref> He earned his [[Ph.D.]] in 2025 in international relations. His doctoral dissertation was titled, ''The Rise and Fall of Paradiplomacy in Australia: Victoria's Engagement with China and the Federal Government's Response''.<ref>{{cite web |title=ISHIDA, Takato |url=https://grips.repo.nii.ac.jp/records/2000263 |access-date=1 October 2026 |website=政策研究大学院大学学術機関リポジトリ |publisher=[[National Graduate Institute for Policy Studies]] |language=ja,en}}</ref> 

While studying abroad, the [[2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami]] prompted him to return to Japan. During a subsequent stay in [[Boston]], [[Massachusetts]], he met a [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Japan)|Ministry of Foreign Affairs]] diplomat who told him he would be well suited to the ministry, prompting him to seek a diplomatic career.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://shingakunet.com/gakko/SC000190/senpaiShigoto/9002322057/|title=関西外国語大学での学びは、外交官になるための力を育んでくれました|language=ja|website=Shingakunet}}</ref>

== Political career ==
=== Ministry of Foreign Affairs ===
[[File:Takato Ishida lecturing at Toyama Prefectural Toyama Minami High School, 2021.jpg|thumb|upright=1|Ishida on a video call lecturing students at Toyama Prefectural Toyama Minami High School in 2021.]]
Ishida passed the Ministry of Foreign Affairs recruitment examination on his third attempt and joined the ministry in 2015. In 2018, he was posted to the Embassy of Japan in the Republic of Zambia as Third Secretary.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://coki.jp/article/column/67548/|title=イケメン知事と話題　福井県知事選で石田嵩人氏35歳が初当選　外務省出身の全国最年少現職|language=ja|date=27 January 2026|author=Yoshida, Konomi|website=Coki}}</ref> While there, he served as an interpreter for a visiting Japanese parliamentary vice minister for foreign affairs during meetings with President Edgar Lungu and for a prime ministerial envoy on an official trip to Nigeria. From 2020 to 2022, he served as Vice Consul at the [[Consulate-General of Japan]] in [[Melbourne]], Australia.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXZQOCC252DI0V20C26A1000000/|title=福井県知事に元官僚の石田嵩人氏初当選　最年少35歳、保守分裂制す|language=ja|date=25 January 2026|website=[[The Nikkei]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://mainichi.jp/articles/20260126/dde/041/010/011000c|title=福井知事選　全国最年少35歳、石田氏が初当選|language=ja|date=26 January 2026|website=[[Mainichi Shimbun]]}}</ref> During his time at the Foreign Ministry, he also worked on issues including [[energy security]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.web.nhk/newsweb/na/nb-3050022406|title=福井県知事選挙　元外務省職員の石田嵩人氏が立候補表明|language=ja|date=25 December 2025|website=[[NHK]]}}</ref>

=== Governor of Fukui Prefecture ===
[[File:2026 Fukui Gubernatorial Election.svg|thumb|upright=1|Results of the 2026 Fukui gubernatorial election, in which Ishida (in orange) won 47.97% of the vote.]]
On 25 December 2025, Ishida held a press conference to announce his resignation from ministerial office in order to run as a candidate for the Governorship of Fukui Prefecture.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.asahi.com/articles/ASTDT2D4CTDTOXIE019M.html|title=元外務省の石田氏が福井知事選に立候補表明　保守系支援で自民分裂も|language=ja|date=25 December 2025|website=[[The Asahi Shimbun]]|author=Oda, Kenji}}</ref> The incumbent governor, [[Tatsuji Sugimoto]], had resigned on 5 December amid allegations of sexual harassment of government employees.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.asahi.com/articles/ASTDW4WFMTDWPTIL00KM.html|title=福井知事選、保守分裂招いた背景は　独自に候補者探った元参院議長|language=ja|date=29 December 2025|author1=Kubo, Tomoyoshi|author2=Oda, Kenji|website=[[The Asahi Shimbun]]}}</ref> While the [[Liberal Democratic Party (Japan)|Liberal Democratic Party]]'s members of the Fukui Prefectural Assembly endorsed former [[Echizen, Fukui|Echizen]] mayor Ken'ichi Yamada, a faction of LDP‑aligned [[Fukui (city)|Fukui City Council]] members who had initially supported Sugimoto instead backed Ishida.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.asahi.com/articles/ASTDW36F9TDWOXIE01BM.html|title=福井知事選、自民は一本化ならず保守分裂　元越前市長らの推薦見送り|language=ja|date=27 December 2025|website=[[The Asahi Shimbun]]|author1=Kubo, Tomoyoshi|author2=Oda, Kenji}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.asahi.com/ajw/articles/16309319|title= Fukui Prefecture elects Ishida as Japan’s youngest governor |date=26 January 2026|author=Kamauchi, Yuki|website=[[The Asahi Shimbun]]}}</ref> Formerly a member of the [[Democratic Party For the People]], Ishida had become an independent and an LDP associate shortly before his announcement.

During the campaign, Ishida used social media to gain support and pledged to expand child‑rearing assistance and strengthen crisis management. Near the campaign's end, [[Sanseitō]] prefectural head Sohei Kamiya announced his backing of Ishida.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.asahi.com/ajw/articles/16311916|title= Sanseito boosted by Fukui victory ahead of Lower House election |date=27 January 2026|website=[[The Asahi Shimbun]]|author=Sugawara, Amane}}</ref> In the 25 January 2026 election, Ishida defeated Kenichi Yamada and Yukie Kanemoto, the latter an official of the [[Japanese Communist Party]]'s prefectural branch, becoming Japan's youngest governor.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/01/26/japan/politics/35-year-old-elected-fukui-governor/|title=35-year-old independent elected as Fukui governor|date=26 January 2026|website=[[The Japan Times]]}}</ref>

After assuming office on 28 January 2026, a greeting video he posted to Instagram went viral, drawing attention and admiration for his appearance and youth, with a subsequent post in March also attracting praise.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.scmp.com/week-asia/people/article/3346240/japans-so-handsome-youngest-governor-36-sets-social-media-abuzz-again|title=Japan’s ‘so handsome’ youngest governor, 36, sets social media abuzz again|date=11 March 2026|website=[[South China Morning Post]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.8days.sg/entertainment/asian/japan-youngest-governor-good-looking-853346|title= This 35-Year-Old Just Became Japan’s Youngest Governor & The Internet’s Latest Crush |date=29 January 2026|author=Wong, Bryan|website=[[8days]]}}</ref> In March 2026, Ishida apologized for a campaign remark describing Japan as "ethnically homogeneous", saying his experience abroad had led him to recognize that Japan is relatively compact in ethnicity, culture, and language.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tokyo-np.co.jp/article/474489|title= 福井知事「単一民族国家」で謝罪　「軽率な発言だった」 |language=ja|date=12 March 2026|website=[[Tokyo Shimbun]]}}</ref>

'''Dulce Soledad Ibarra''' (born 1991) is an American multidisciplinary artist, educator, [[curator]], and activist. Ibarra's pronouns are they/them/theirs. They are [[Hispanic and Latino Americans|Latinx]], and their work explores ethnicity, identity, class, labor, and the immigrant experience in the United States. Ibarra has worked in sculpture, installation art, performance art, video and new media art, illustration, and textiles. They lives in Los Angeles.<ref name="Dávila-2020">{{Cite book |last=Dávila |first=Arlene |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ngTzDwAAQBAJ |title=Latinx Art: Artists, Markets, and Politics |date=July 24, 2020 |publisher=[[Duke University Press]] |isbn=978-1-4780-0885-9 |pages=208 |language=en}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Dulce Soledad Ibarra was born in 1991, in [[Chino, California]].<ref name="Dávila-2020" /> They are queer, and used the pronouns they/them/theirs.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Madre Myths |url=https://msjc.edu/artgallery/Madre-Myths.html |access-date=2026-04-05 |website=Mt. San Jacinto College|quote=Dulce Soledad Ibarra (they/them/theirs)... Looking through queer Xicanx perspective...}}</ref>{{Better source needed|reason=The current source is insufficiently reliable ([[WP:NOTRS]]).|date=April 2026}}

Ibarra received a [[Bachelor of Fine Arts]] degree in 2017 in sculpture from the [[California State University, Long Beach]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2019-11-27 |title=ART GALLERY EXHIBITION: 5th Sur:biennial |url=https://www.lbcc.edu/arts/art-gallery-exhibition-5th-surbiennial |access-date=2026-02-10 |website=Long Beach City College |language=en}}</ref> They continued her studies at the Roski School of Art and Design at the [[University of Southern California]] (USC), and graduated with a [[Master of Fine Arts]] degree in 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dulce Soledad Ibarra MFA Thesis Project |url=https://calendar.usc.edu/event/dulce_soledad_ibarra_mfa_thesis_project |access-date=2026-02-10 |website=Event Calendar |language=en}}</ref> 

While attending undergrad they started to explore artistic themes of identity, assimilation, and the relationship of [[generational trauma]] found in Latino families.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Lawler |first1=Natalie |last2=Johnson |first2=Denise |last3=Herse |first3=Marcus |last4=Bocinski |first4=Jessica |last5=Wogahn |first5=Manon |date=2017-09-01 |title=MyBarrio: Emigdio Vasquez and Chicana/o Identity in Orange County |url=https://digitalcommons.chapman.edu/university_art_exhibition_catalogs/1 |journal=Exhibition Catalogs}}</ref> During the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|COVID-19 pandemic]], Ibarra explored the digital art and performance art for their practice.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-11-04 |title=Now More Than Ever: The Need for Alternative Cultural Spaces |url=https://www.pbssocal.org/shows/artbound/now-more-than-ever-the-need-for-alternative-cultural-spaces |access-date=2026-02-25 |website=PBS SoCal |language=en}}</ref> After their time receiving education, Ibarra created a career as a working artist, and curator.<ref>{{Cite web |title=EPHE-MORIZED {{!}} Mt. San Jacinto College |url=https://msjc.edu/artgallery/EPHE-MORIZED.html |access-date=2026-02-25 |website=msjc.edu}}</ref> Beginning in 2021, they started teaching at [[Mt. San Jacinto College|Mount San Jacinto College]] in Riverside County, California.<ref name="Rotell">{{Cite web |last=Rotell |first=Mia |title=The History and Mind Behind Dulce Soledad Ibarra's Madre Myths |url=https://msjctalonnews.com/8071/msjc/the-history-and-mind-behind-dulce-soledad-ibarras-madre-myths/ |access-date=2026-02-10 |website=The Talon Student News|date=October 6, 2023}}</ref>

Ibarra has been recognized for their dedication to smaller spaces and communities.<ref name="Oduga-2024">{{Cite web |title=A Los Angeles Residency Envisions a Radical Future for Experimental Art |url=https://hyperallergic.com/a-los-angeles-residency-envisions-a-radical-future-for-experimental-art/ |access-date=2026-02-10 |website=[[Hyperallergic]] |date=March 26, 2024 |last=Oduga |first=Joshua}}</ref>

'''Paul Anthony Kelly''' (born October 1, 1988) is a Canadian model and actor based in the United States. He is best known for portraying [[John F. Kennedy Jr.]] in the first season of the [[FX (TV channel)|FX]] anthology miniseries ''[[Love Story (2026 TV series)|Love Story: John F. Kennedy Jr. & Carolyn Bessette]]''.

== Early life and career ==
Kelly was born in the small Canadian town of [[Port McNicoll, Ontario]], on October 1, 1988.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://harpersbazaar.my/lifestyle/fun-facts-about-paul-anthony-kelly-from-love-story/|title=Fun Facts About Paul Anthony Kelly From “Love Story”|work=[[Harper's Bazaar]] Malaysia|date=February 19, 2026|last=Salehaldin|first=Syameen}}</ref><ref name=intmag>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.interviewmagazine.com/culture/paul-anthony-kelly-tells-mel-ottenberg-how-he-became-john-john|title=Paul Anthony Kelly Tells Mel Ottenberg How He Became John-John|work=[[Interview (magazine)|Interview]]|date=December 17, 2025|last=Ottenberg|first=Mel}}</ref> He is the eldest of four children. He later moved to [[Toronto]] and while working at [[American Apparel]], he was discovered by two talent scouts and began modelling after signing a contract with [[Ford Models]].<ref name=ang>{{cite web |last1=Ang |first1=Raymond |title=How Love Story’s Paul Anthony Kelly Became JFK Jr. |url=https://www.gq.com/story/how-love-storys-paul-anthony-kelly-became-jfk-jr |website=GQ |date=24 February 2026}}</ref> From there he moved to [[New York City]], where he began auditioning for acting roles whilst still working as a model, signing with the agency Innovative Artists.<ref name=intmag/><ref name=":0">{{cite web|url=https://www.scmp.com/magazines/style/people/celebrities/article/3338176/meet-paul-anthony-kelly-who-plays-john-f-kennedy-jr-ryan-murphys-love-story|title=
Meet Paul Anthony Kelly, who plays John F. Kennedy Jr in Ryan Murphy’s Love Story|work=South China Morning Post|date=February 14, 2026|last=Sarkar|first=Ishani}}</ref> He did not find work in acting for a decade, except for a project called ''[[The Venery of Samantha Bird]]'', which was ultimately never released in part due to the [[2023 SAG-AFTRA strike]].<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/heels-canceled-plus-three-more-starz-shows-1235598872/|title=Starz Cancels Three Series and Scraps Another|work=The Hollywood Reporter|date=September 25, 2023|last=O'Connell|first=Mikey}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/entertainment/celebrities/2026/02/19/paul-kelly-anthony-love-story-jfk-jr-internet-obsession/88744522007/|title='Love Story' star Paul Kelly Anthony has the internet obsessed. See why.|work=USA Today|last=Shafiq|first=Saman|date=February 19, 2026}}</ref> As a model, he worked for brands like [[Rhone Apparel]], [[Vivienne Westwood]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://models.com/work/vivienne-westwood-vivienne-westwood-man-ss-14-mens-show-milan|title=Vivienne Westwood SS/14 Men's Show|work=models.com}}</ref> [[Bonobos (apparel)|Bonobos]], [[John Varvatos]], [[Loro Piana]], [[Perry Ellis]], and [[Brooks Brothers]].<ref name=intmag/><ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.harpersbazaar.com/culture/film-tv/g65511599/american-love-story-carolyn-bessette-jfk-jr-cast-characters/|title=The Cast of Love Story Compared to Their Real-Life Counterparts|last=Dixon|first=Lucy|date=February 12, 2026|magazine=Harper's Bazaar}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wmagazine.com/culture/american-love-story-carolyn-bessette-kennedy-jfk-jr-cast-release-date-trailer-plot|title=Everything to Know About Ryan Murphy’s American Love Story|last=McCartney|first=Claire Valentine|date=March 25, 2025|website=W Magazine}}</ref>

Despite having no professional acting experience, he was cast as [[John F. Kennedy Jr.]] in ''[[Love Story (2026 TV series)|Love Story]]'' shortly before filming was scheduled to commence.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tvguide.com/news/love-story-john-f-kennedy-jr-actor-paul-anthony-kelly/|title=FX's Love Story Almost Pushed Back Filming Because They Didn't Have a John F. Kennedy Jr. Then Came Paul Anthony Kelly|date=February 14, 2026|last=Moon|first=Kat|work=TV Guide}}</ref> He was cast after a successful chemistry read and screen test with [[Sarah Pidgeon]].<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.vogue.com/article/love-story-john-f-kennedy-jr-and-carolyn-bessette-sarah-pidgeon-paul-kelly-interview|title=Meet the Star-Crossed Leads of Love Story: John F. Kennedy Jr. & Carolyn Bessette|work=Vogue|date=February 12, 2026|last=Seth|first=Radhika|publisher=Condé Nast}}</ref>

In June 2026, it was announced Kelly would star in ''The Housemaid's Secret'', alongside [[Sydney Sweeney]] and [[Kirsten Dunst]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Grobar |first=Matt |date=2026-06-11 |title=Paul Anthony Kelly Joins 'The Housemaid's Secret' In Film Debut |url=https://deadline.com/2026/06/paul-anthony-kelly-joins-the-housemaids-secret-1236953707/ |access-date=2026-06-12 |website=Deadline |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Kelly married Syd Widziszewski in May 2023,<ref name=":1">{{cite web|url=https://www.mundoamerica.com/celebrity/2026/02/19/6996f61521efa0fa178b45a2.html|title=Sir John F. Kennedy Jr.: the great opportunity that Canadian actor Paul Anthony Kelly has been waiting for|work=[[El Mundo (Spain)|El Mundo]]|last=Pedrejón|first=Isabel|date=February 19, 2026}}</ref> with whom he had his first child in early 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wayman |first=Sasha |date=2026-02-25 |title=Love Story’s Paul Anthony Kelly Welcomes First Baby with Wife Syd Widziszewski-Kelly |url=https://www.eonline.com/news/1428951/love-storys-paul-anthony-kelly-welcomes-baby-with-syd-widziszewski-kelly |access-date=2026-03-12 |website=E! Online}}</ref> They live in [[Portland, Oregon]],<ref name=":0" /> having previously lived in [[California]].<ref name=":1" /> Kelly is a [[green card|permanent resident]] of the United States as of 2025.<ref name="intmag" />

[[Home Depot]] (2025–present) | children = 3 | website = {{url|https://news.xbox.com/en-us/leadership/asha-sharma/|Official website}} }} '''Asha Sharma''' (born 1989) is an American business executive who serves as [[executive vice president]] (EVP) and [[chief executive officer]] (CEO) of [[Xbox (division)|Xbox]].{{Cite web |last=Warren |first=Tom |date=2026-04-23 |title=Microsoft brings Xbox back, scraps Microsoft Gaming |url=https://www.theverge.com/report/917485/microsoft-return-of-xbox-no-more-microsoft-gaming |access-date=2026-04-23 |website=The Verge |language=en-US}} She succeeded [[Phil Spencer (business executive)|Phil Spencer]] on February 20, 2026. Previously, Sharma served as [[Microsoft]]'s corporate vice president and head of product for its AI platform from 2024 to 2025. She also worked as president of its CoreAI product organization from 2025 to 2026.{{Cite web |title=Board of Directors |url=https://ir.homedepot.com/corporate-governance/board-of-directors |access-date=2026-09-14 |website=ir.homedepot.com |language=en}} == Early life == Sharma was born in [[Racine, Wisconsin]], in 1989. She is of Indian [[Punjabis|Punjabi]] descent.{{Cite news |last=Rajghatta |first=Chidanand |author-link=Chidanand Rajghatta |date=21 February 2026 |title=Ctrl+Alt+Elite: Microsoft hands Xbox controller to Asha Sharma |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/international-business/ctrlaltelite-microsoft-hands-xbox-controller-to-asha-sharma/articleshow/128647822.cms |access-date=2026-07-18 |work=[[The Times of India]] |issn=0971-8257 |quote=In a sweeping reset during Xbox’s 25th anniversary year, Satya Nadella-led Microsoft has named Asha Sharma as CEO of Microsoft Gaming, pitching another Indian-American into a leadership position at a time of intense xenophobia in MAGA circles. ... For many, it is another milestone in the continued ascent of Indian-origin executives in Silicon Valley who remain uninhibited in the face of MAGA paranoia. Still, the appointment has unfolded in a fraught political moment. Online, some MAGA-aligned voices have recycled claims of corporate nepotism and "favoring their own," casting Sharma as part of an "Indian tech-bro" archetype.}} Her parents had immigrated to the United States from [[New Zealand]] and settled in Racine near relatives. Her parents were divorced, and her mother worked at a department store. As a teenager, Sharma worked on a golf course.{{cite web |last1=Ray |first1=Tiernan |date=March 1, 2018 |title=‘We Must Be Heroes to Girls and Women,’ Says Facebook Exec |url=https://www.barrons.com/articles/we-must-be-heroes-to-girls-and-women-says-facebook-exec-1519932602 |website=Barron's |language=en-US |access-date=April 22, 2026}} Her father worked for a family-owned metal fabrication business while completing an engineering degree, and Sharma has credited his approach to work with influencing her own attitude toward school, employment, and extracurricular activities.{{Cite news |last=Fritz |first=Ben |date=2026-09-12 |title=The Woman Fixing a Microsoft Mess With Brutal Honesty |url=https://www.wsj.com/tech/xbox-microsoft-asha-sharma-videogame-03eb23ba |access-date=2026-09-12 |work=Wall Street Journal |language=en-US |issn=0099-9660}} During her teenage years, Sharma considered pursuing medicine and envisioned combining it with her interest in sports by working as a physician for the [[Green Bay Packers]]. She subsequently attended the [[University of Minnesota]], where she studied business. While in college, she completed several internships, participated in academic research projects in [[Hungary]] and [[Poland]], and helped establish a nonprofit organization that raised around $500,000. She earned a [[Bachelor of Science]] degree in business from the [[Carlson School of Management]] at the [[University of Minnesota]], graduating in 2011.{{cite web |last1=Rupard |first1=Wade |date=October 14, 2022 |title=Executive Spotlight: Instacart COO Asha Sharma |url=https://carlsonschool.umn.edu/news/executive-spotlight-instacart-coo-asha-sharma |website=Carlson School of Management |publisher=University of Minnesota |language=en-US |access-date=March 24, 2026}}{{cite web |title=Two U of M Alumni Named among Forbes 30 Under 30 |url=https://twin-cities.umn.edu/news-events/two-u-m-alumni-named-among-forbes-30-under-30 |website=Carlson School of Management |publisher=University of Minnesota |language=en-US |date=January 14, 2015 |access-date=March 24, 2026}} While she was a student, Sharma launched and led a center for at-risk teenagers called the A-list in Brooklyn Park, which closed soon after her departure.{{Cite web |last=Kumar |first=Kavita |date=September 5, 2015 |title=Sunday conversation with Asha Sharma of Porch, an online home services portal |url=https://www.startribune.com/sunday-conversation-with-asha-sharma-of-porch-an-online-home-services-portal/324476061 |website=The Minnesota Star Tribune |language=en-US |access-date=March 24, 2026}} == Career == === Microsoft and Porch === Sharma began her career at [[S.C. Johnson]] at the age of 17. After graduating from the University of Minnesota, she joined [[Microsoft]]’s marketing department in 2011. In 2013, she joined [[Porch (company)|Porch]], a home services technology company, where she eventually became chief operating officer.{{Cite web |last=Gesenhues |first=Amy |date=2014-07-02 |title=Get To Know: Porch.com CMO Asha Sharma |url=https://martech.org/get-know-porch-com-cmo-asha/ |website=martech}} === Facebook === In 2017, Sharma joined [[Meta Platforms|Facebook]], where she held senior product leadership roles, including vice president of product for [[Facebook Messenger|Messenger]] and other private communications products across Facebook and [[Instagram]].{{Cite web |title=AppLovin Adds Instacart Chief Operating Officer Asha Sharma to Its Board of Directors |url=https://investors.applovin.com/news/news-details/2021/AppLovin-Adds-Instacart-Chief-Operating-Officer-Asha-Sharma-to-Its-Board-of-Directors/default.aspx |access-date=2026-09-14 |website=investors.applovin.com |language=en-US}} === Instacart (2021–2024) === Sharma joined [[Instacart]] as chief operating officer (COO) in June 2021. She remained in the position until March 2024. In September 2025, she became president of Microsoft’s CoreAI product organization.{{Cite web |last=McCaffrey |first=Ryan |date=February 20, 2026 |title=Phil Spencer Retiring, Sarah Bond Out, Matt Booty Promoted as Microsoft AI Exec Asha Sharma Named New Xbox Boss – EXCLUSIVE |url= https://www.ign.com/articles/phil-spencer-retiring-sarah-bond-out-matt-booty-promoted-as-microsoft-ai-exec-asha-sharma-named-new-xbox-boss-exclusive |website=IGN |language=en-US |access-date=March 24, 2026}} On February 20, 2026, Sharma was announced as executive vice president and CEO of Microsoft Gaming following the retirement of [[Phil Spencer (business executive)|Phil Spencer]]. Her selection came as a surprise, passing over Spencer's second-in-command [[Sarah Bond (executive)|Sarah Bond]]. Sharma received scrutiny for having no professional experience in the video game industry prior to her appointment to lead [[Xbox]]. Sharma's history in user acquisition was a primary motivator for her selection, as Xbox has seen declining console sales over recent years. In a statement following her appointment, Sharma promised to "recommit to our core Xbox fans and players" and "not chase short-term efficiency or flood our ecosystem with soulless [[AI slop]].” On She has three children. She became a stepmother before she and her husband had two children of their own. She has spoken about the challenge of balancing the demands of an executive career with raising a family and has said that her personal life has taught her to become more comfortable with uncertainty. She has cited Indian-American businesswoman [[Indra Nooyi]] as an inspiration.{{Cite web |date=21 April 2023 |title=40 Under 40: Asha Sharma, Instacart |url=https://www.bizjournals.com/sanfrancisco/news/2023/04/21/asha-sharma-instacart.html |access-date=2026-07-18 |website=[[San Francisco Business Times]] |language=en-US}} Sharma is a second-degree black belt in [[taekwondo]].{{cite podcast |host=Lenny Rachitsky |date=August 28, 2025 |title=How 80,000 companies build with AI: Products as organisms and the death of org charts - Asha Sharma |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=J9UWaltU-7Q }} She posted in 2026 that she had recently begun playing video games under the gamertag AMRAHSAHSA to "learn and understand" the games industry.{{Cite tweet |author=Asha Sharma |user=asha_shar |date=2026-02-23 |title=I also didn't expect my gamertag to blowup and the reality is more boring. '''Akari Fukunishi''' (born 23 November 1990) is a Japanese [[ice sledge hockey]] player. She was the only woman to compete at the [[2026 Winter Olympics]] in [[Para ice hockey at the 2026 Winter Paralympics|para ice hockey]].

== Biography ==
In March 2021, while riding her motorcycle, Akari was struck by a car, leading to a critical injury. She regained mobility but lost the ability to run or jump.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-10-23 |title=Para Ice Hockey: A Groundbreaking Journey for Women in Sports |url=https://japandaily.jp/para-ice-hockey-a-groundbreaking-journey-for-women-in-sports/ |access-date=2026-06-25 |website=Japan Daily |language=en-US}}</ref>

At the [[2025 Women's World Para Ice Hockey Championships|2025 Women's World Para Ice Hockey Championship]] in Slovakia, the inaugural edition of the tournament, Akari played for Team World. Team World was composed of players who do not have their own national team.<ref>{{Cite web |title=In para ice hockey, a tentative move towards mixed teams before a 100% female tournament? |url=https://www.francsjeux.com/en/2026/03/10/Milan-Cortina-2026-in-para-ice-hockey%3A-a-tentative-mix-of-genders-before-a-100%25-women%27s-tournament/109531/ |access-date=2026-06-25 |website=Francs Jeux |language=en}}</ref>

Akari was the only woman to compete at the [[2026 Winter Olympics]] in [[Para ice hockey at the 2026 Winter Paralympics|para ice hockey]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-03-09 |title=Paralympics: Japan women make milestone debuts in ice hockey, snowboard |url=https://english.kyodonews.net/articles/-/71925 |access-date=2026-03-10 |website=Japan Wire by KYODO NEWS |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-03-10 |title=Winter Paralympics 2026: The 'mixed' team event with one woman |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/ice-hockey/articles/cp81498elp4o |access-date=2026-03-10 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Kennedy |first=Ian |date=2026-03-09 |title=Akari Fukunishi Is The Only Woman Competing In Para Ice Hockey At The 2026 Paralympics As She Carries The Torch For All Women |url=https://thehockeynews.com/womens/international/akari-fukunishi-is-the-only-woman-competing-in-para-ice-hockey-at-the-2026-paralympics-as-she-carries-the-torch-for-all-women |access-date=2026-03-10 |website=The Hockey News |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=福西 朱莉｜ミラノ・コルティナパラ アイスホッケーの注目選手｜パラサポWEB |url=https://www.parasapo.tokyo/featured-athletes/fukunishi-akari |access-date=2026-06-25 |website=パラサポWEB |language=ja}}</ref> She the fourth woman to take part in para ice hockey in the history of the [[Paralympic Games|Paralympics]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Three players, one shared dream: a Paralympic women’s Para ice hockey tournament |url=https://www.paralympic.org/news/three-players-one-dream-paralympic-women-para-ice-hockey-tournament |access-date=2026-06-25 |website=International Paralympic Committee |language=en}}</ref>

He subsequently defended the title multiple times, including a match against [[Jay Bradley]] for NWA Southeast in April 2024.{{cite web |title=Sanctioned NWA Territories |url=https://www.nationalwrestlingalliance.com/nwaterritories |website=Nationalwrestlingalliance.com |access-date=10 May 2024}} At ''[[NWA Samhain]]'', Mason retained his NWA National Championship by defeating [[Chris Masters|Chris Adonis]].{{cite web |last1=Carey |first1=Ian |title=NWA Samhain notes: EC3 vs. Thom Latimer, Kenzie Paige vs. Ruthie Jay |website=[[MSN]] |url=https://www.msn.com/en-us/sports/other/nwa-samhain-notes-ec3-vs-thom-latimer-kenzie-paige-vs-ruthie-jay/ar-AA1j2Mci |access-date=7 March 2024}} On the March 19th episode of NWA Powerrr, Mason relinquished the NWA National Championship in order to pursue a match with [[Ethan Carter III|EC3]] for the [[NWA Worlds Heavyweight Championship]].{{cite web |last1=Tessier |first1=Colin |title=Silas Mason Relinquishes NWA National Title, New Champion To Be Crowned At NWA Hard Times |date=20 March 2024 |url=https://www.yahoo.com/entertainment/silas-mason-relinquishes-nwa-national-003023109.html |access-date=20 March 2024}} In March 2024, Mason lost his home and possessions in a house fire. A [[GoFundMe]] fundraiser was set up by [[Kerry Morton]] to support Mason following the event.{{cite web |last1=Woodward |first1=Hamish |title=GoFundMe Set Up For NWA's Silas Mason After House Fire |url=https://www.yardbarker.com/wrestling/articles/gofundme_set_up_for_nwas_silas_mason_after_house_fire/s1_16998_40102936 |website=wrestlezone.com |date=13 March 2024 |access-date=13 March 2024}} At [[NWA Hard Times (2024)|NWA Hard Times 2024]], episode 5, which debuted on [[The CW]] app May 7, 2024, Mason was unsuccessful in challenging [[Ethan Carter III|EC3]] for the [[NWA Worlds Heavyweight Championship]]. In the [[Crockett Cup (2024)|2024 Crockett Cup]], Mason teamed up with "The Southern 6" stablemate Kerry Morton and defeated The Slimeballz (Sage Chantz and Tommy Rant) in the first rounds. Mason got injured mid-tournament and had to be replaced by Alex Taylor, with whom Morton won the entire competition. Mason was not recognized as co-winner.{{cite web|url=https://www.fightful.com/wrestling/results/nwa-powerrr-results-716-crockett-cup-finals-nwa-worlds-title-defended|title=NWA Powerrr Results (7/16): Crockett Cup Finals, NWA Worlds Title Defended|work=Fightful|first=Jeremy|last=Lambert|date=July 20, 2024|access-date=July 23, 2024}} The NWA announced on July 18, 2024, that Mason, along with his Southern Six stablemates Kerry Morton and Alex Taylor, had signed exclusive contracts with the NWA. Additionally, it was confirmed that all three members will appear at the ''[[NWA 76th Anniversary Show]]''.{{cite web |title=The Southern Six Win 2024 Crockett Cup, Sign Exclusive NWA Contracts |url=https://www.nationalwrestlingalliance.com/news/the-southern-six-win-crockett-cup-2024-earn-exclusive-nwa-contracts |publisher=[[National Wrestling Alliance]] |date=18 July 2024 |access-date=24 July 2024}} A the ''[[NWA 77th Anniversary Show]]'', Mason defeated [[Thom Latimer]] to become the [[NWA World's Heavyweight Championship|NWA World's Heavyweight champion]], and becoming the first 90's born NWA worlds Heavyweight champion.{{cite web |last1=Martinez |first1=Tommy |title=NWA Powerrr: A 'Thrill'-ing NWA 77 Title Match |url=https://slamwrestling.net/report/nwa-powerrr-a-thrill-ing-nwa-77-title-match/ |website=Slam Wrestling |access-date=24 February 2026}} Mason scored his first pay-per-view defense of the title at ''[[NWA Samhain: Part 3]]'' on January 27, 2026 (aired) by defeating [[Matt Cardona]].{{cite web|url=https://www.fightful.com/wrestling/nwa-samhain-3-results-10-17-silas-mason-defends-nwa-worlds-heavyweight-title/|title=NWA Samhain 3 Results (10/17): Silas Mason Defends NWA Worlds Heavyweight Title|first=Jeremy|last=Lambert|work=Fightful|date=October 19, 2025|access-date=October 26, 2025}} Mason continued to defend and retain the championship at major NWA events such as the [[Crockett Cup (2026)|2026 ''Crockett Cup'']] against [[Bryan Idol]] and ''[[NWA Hard Times 6]]'' against [[Kerry Morton]]. In June 2026, Mason successfully defended his title against [[Shotaro Ashino]] at [[All Japan Pro Wrestling|All Japan Pro Wreslting's]] ''Super Power Series 2026''. '''Delilah Belle Hamlin''' (born June 10, 1998)<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Marsh |first=Ariana |date=April 2, 2025 |title=Who Is Delilah Belle Hamlin? Everything You Need to Know About the Model and Actor |url=https://www.harpersbazaar.com/celebrity/latest/a64366839/who-is-delilah-belle-hamlin/ |access-date= |website=[[Harper's BAZAAR]] |language=}}</ref> is an American [[model (person)|model]], actress, and singer. The eldest daughter of actors [[Harry Hamlin]] and [[Lisa Rinna]], Hamlin began her modeling career at 18, and has modeled for brands such as [[Skims]], [[Michael Kors (brand)|Michael Kors]], and [[Steve Madden, Ltd.|Steve Madden]]. She's appeared on the covers of ''[[Vogue Japan]]'' & [[Vogue Czechoslovakia|''Czechoslovakia'']], and has walked runways for [[Tommy Hilfiger (company)|Tommy Hilfiger]] and [[Dolce & Gabbana]].

== Early life and education ==
Hamlin was born on June 10, 1998, in [[Los Angeles]], [[California]], to actor [[Harry Hamlin]] and actress [[Lisa Rinna]].<ref name=":0" /> She has a younger sister, model [[Amelia Gray Hamlin]], and an older paternal half-brother, Dimitri Alexander Hamlin, the son of Harry Hamlin and Swiss actress [[Ursula Andress]].<ref name="thethings">{{cite web |title=Do Amelia Gray And Delilah Belle Hamlin Live In Each Other's Shadows? |url=https://www.thethings.com/are-amelia-gray-and-sister-delilah-belle-hamlin-close/ |website=TheThings |access-date=March 19, 2026}}</ref><ref name="buzznigeria">{{cite web |title=Life Story of Dimitri Alexander Hamlin, Harry Hamlin's Son |url=https://buzznigeria.com/us/life-story-of-dimitri-alexander-hamlin-harry-hamlins-son/ |website=Buzz Nigeria |access-date=March 19, 2026}}</ref>

She attended Halfstrom Academy, a one-on-one individualized study program in Los Angeles, and graduated from high school in June 2017.<ref name="wwd-img">{{cite web |title=IMG Models Signs Delilah Belle Hamlin |url=https://wwd.com/feature/img-models-signs-delilah-belle-hamlin-10864227/ |website=[[Women's Wear Daily|WWD]] |date=April 2017 |access-date=March 19, 2026}}</ref> In January 2018, she enrolled at [[New York University]] to study criminal psychology, but withdrew shortly afterward due to mental health difficulties.<ref name="paper-nyfw">{{cite web |title=Delilah Belle on NYFW and Growing Up in the Limelight |url=https://www.papermag.com/delilah-belle-nyfw |website=[[Paper (magazine)|Paper]] |date=5 February 2019 |access-date=March 19, 2026|last=Bennett|first=Willa}}</ref>

== Career ==
In 2010, when Hamlin was 12, she made her television debut in her parents' 2010 reality series ''[[Harry Loves Lisa]]'', which followed her parents' family life.<ref name="tvmaze">{{cite web |title=Harry Loves Lisa |url=https://www.tvmaze.com/shows/27625/harry-loves-lisa |website=TVmaze |access-date=March 19, 2026}}</ref> Subsequently, she appeared in approximately 45 episodes of ''[[The Real Housewives of Beverly Hills]]'' (2014–2022) during her mother's tenure as a main cast member.<ref name="primetimer">{{cite web |title=The Traitors' Lisa Rinna's daughters Delilah and Amelia Hamlin: How they built careers beyond reality TV |url=https://www.primetimer.com/features/the-traitors-lisa-rinnas-daughters-delilah-and-amelia-hamlin-how-they-built-careers-beyond-reality-tv |website=Primetimer |date=January 2026 |access-date=March 19, 2026}}</ref>

Hamlin was discovered through [[Instagram]] when modeling agencies noticed her posts.<ref name="wwd-img" /> In August 2016, Hamlin signed with [[Elite Model Management]].<ref name="wmag-model">{{cite web |title=Delilah Belle Hamlin Is the Next Millennial Model to Watch |url=https://www.wmagazine.com/story/delilah-belle-hamlin-model |website=[[W (magazine)|W Magazine]] |access-date=March 19, 2026|date=March 10, 2017|last=McCarthy|first=Lauren}}</ref> The same month, she appeared in an editorial for ''[[Teen Vogue]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gaynor |first=Emily |date=August 10, 2016 |title=Get to Know Teen Model and Singer Delilah Belle Hamlin |url=https://www.teenvogue.com/gallery/delilah-belle-hamlin-models-2000s-fashion-beauty-trends |access-date=September 1, 2026 |website=[[Teen Vogue]] |language=}}</ref> She would make her runway debut the following month at [[New York Fashion Week]], walking in the [[Tommy Hilfiger]] × [[Gigi Hadid]] fashion show.<ref name="bravo-tommy">{{cite web |title=NYFW: Tommy Hilfiger Gigi Hadid Show: Lisa Rinna's Daughter Walks |url=https://www.bravotv.com/the-daily-dish/new-york-fashion-week-lisa-rinna-daughter-walked-tommy-hilfiger-fashion-show |website=[[Bravo (American TV network)|Bravo TV]] |access-date=March 19, 2026}}</ref> In February 2017, she walked in [[Milan Fashion Week]] for [[Dolce & Gabbana]] in the Baja East runway.<ref name="wmag-dg">{{cite web |title=Delilah Belle Hamlin Has No Drama with Gigi Hadid, But Did Learn to Model From Her |url=https://www.wmagazine.com/story/delilah-belle-hamlin-gigi-hadid-dolce-gabbana-lisa-rinna |website=[[W (magazine)|W Magazine]] |access-date=March 19, 2026}}</ref> In March, she appeared in a editorial for ''[[W (magazine)|W Magazine]]'', which described her as "the Next Millennial Model to Watch".<ref name="wmag-model" /> In April, she signed with [[IMG Models]].<ref name="wwd-img" />

In April 2025, Hamlin collaborated with Ukrainian brand Guzema to create the "Metamorphosis" jewelry capsule.<ref name="jck-guzema">{{cite web |title=Guzema Evokes Hope for a New Era With Metamorphosis |url=https://www.jckonline.com/editorial-article/guzema-metamorphosis/ |website=JCK |access-date=March 19, 2026}}</ref><ref name="yahoo-guzema">{{cite web |title=Delilah Belle Hamlin Debuts Jewelry Capsule Collection With Guzema Inspired by Her 'Butterfly' Era and Y2K Trends |url=https://www.yahoo.com/lifestyle/delilah-belle-hamlin-debuts-jewelry-040000102.html |website=[[Yahoo!]] |access-date=March 19, 2026}}</ref> In July 2025, both she and her sister modeled for their ''[[V (American magazine)|V Magazine]]'' profile.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 2, 2025 |title=V155: Fellini Underground with Amelia Gray & Delilah Belle |url=https://vmagazine.com/article/v155-fellini-underground-with-amelia-gray-delilah-belle/ |access-date=September 1, 2026 |website=[[V (American magazine)|V Magazine]] |language=}}</ref> Together, the sisters then modeled for [[H&M]]'s Summer 2025 campaign.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |title=AMELIA GRAY AND DELILAH BELLE - == Personal life ==

=== Relationships ===
Hamlin dated [[Love Island (British TV series)|''Love Island UK'']] contestant Eyal Booker from April 2019 to late 2021. The couple were first linked publicly at [[Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival|Coachella]] and confirmed their relationship in May 2019.<ref name="refinery29">{{cite web |title=Lisa Rinna Daughter Delilah Is Dating Love Island Star |url=https://www.refinery29.com/en-us/2021/07/10578159/who-is-delilah-hamlin-boyfriend-eyal-love-island |website=[[Refinery29]] |access-date=March 19, 2026}}</ref><ref name="enews-breakup">{{cite web |title=Delilah Belle Hamlin and Love Island's Eyal Booker Break Up After 2 Years Together |url=https://www.eonline.com/news/1315797/delilah-belle-hamlin-and-love-islands-eyal-booker-break-up-after-2-years-together |website=[[E! News]] |date=January 2022 |access-date=March 19, 2026}}</ref> In 2023, she began dating actor Henry Eikenberry, known for ''[[Euphoria (American TV series)|Euphoria]]''; the pair made their red carpet debut in June 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bellusci |first=Alexandra |date=June 2, 2023 |title=Lisa Rinna's Daughter Delilah Hamlin Makes Red Carpet Debut With Actor Henry Eikenberry |url=https://www.eonline.com/news/1376211/lisa-rinnas-daughter-delilah-hamlin-makes-red-carpet-debut-with-actor-henry-eikenberry |access-date=September 1, 2026 |website=[[E! Online]]}}</ref>

=== Health ===
Hamlin was diagnosed with [[PANDAS]] as a child, which led to severe anxiety and panic attacks beginning around age 11.<ref name="bravo-health">{{cite web |title=Delilah Belle Hamlin Opens Up About Her Health Issues |url=https://www.bravotv.com/the-daily-dish/rhobh-lisa-rinnas-daughter-delilah-opens-up-about-her-health |website=[[Bravo (American TV network)|Bravo TV]] |access-date=March 19, 2026}}</ref> Upon her enrollment at New York University, Hamlin began suffering with depression. Eight months later, she returned to Los Angeles and entered a [[rehabilitation center]] for mental health issues.<ref name=":0" />

In November 2021, Hamlin was hospitalized following an accidental [[Alprazolam|xanax]] [[Drug overdose|overdose]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kirkpatrick |first=Emily |date=November 3, 2021 |title=Lisa Rinna's Daughter Delilah Belle Hamlin Hospitalized After Accidental Overdose |url=https://www.vanityfair.com/style/2021/11/delilah-belle-hamlin-hospitalized-accidental-overdose-xanax-instagram-live-lisa-rinna-harry-hamlin |access-date= |website=[[Vanity Fair (magazine)|Vanity Fair]] |language=en-US}}</ref> She later said that she had previously been diagnosed with [[Lyme disease]], [[Epstein–Barr virus]], and [[encephalitis]], and explained the accidental overdose resulting from prescribed [[benzodiazepine]] medication.<ref name="enews-xanax">{{cite web |title=Delilah Belle Hamlin Says She Sought Treatment After Becoming "Dependent" on Xanax |url=https://www.eonline.com/news/1308126/delilah-belle-hamlin-says-she-sought-treatment-after-becoming-dependent-on-xanax |website=[[E! News]] |date=November 2021 |access-date=March 19, 2026}}</ref><ref name="newsweek">{{cite web |title=Who Is Delilah Belle Hamlin? Lisa Rinna and Harry Hamlin's Daughter |url=https://www.newsweek.com/who-delilah-belle-hamlin-lisa-rinna-1645443 |website=[[Newsweek]] |date=November 2021 |access-date=March 19, 2026}}</ref> She achieved sobriety in mid-2021 and publicly celebrated six months sober in February 2022.<ref name="et-sober">{{cite web |title=Delilah Belle Hamlin marks 6 months of sobriety after accidental overdose |url=https://www.yahoo.com/entertainment/delilah-belle-hamlin-marks-6-months-sobriety-174406161.html |website=[[Yahoo!]] |access-date=March 19, 2026}}</ref>

In 2025, she disclosed a diagnosis of [[endometriosis]] and underwent surgery in August of that year. She discussed her experience on the ''She MD'' podcast in December 2025, noting that the condition had been linked to her seizures.<ref name="yahoo-endo">{{cite web |title=Delilah Belle Hamlin Details "Painful" Endometriosis Journey |url=https://www.yahoo.com/entertainment/celebrity/articles/delilah-belle-hamlin-details-painful-210801463.html |website=[[Yahoo!]] |access-date=March 19, 2026}}</ref><ref name="onda-health">{{cite web |title=Delilah Belle Hamlin Opens Up About Her Health Struggles And Triumphs |url=https://onda.la/news/delilah-belle-hamlin-opens-up-about-her-health-struggles-and-triumphs-12122025/ |website=ONDA LA |date=December 12, 2025 |access-date=March 19, 2026}}</ref>

'''Marcel Alcalá''' (born 1990) is an American multidisciplinary visual artist. They work in painting,<ref name="Stone-2021">{{Cite web |last=Stone |first=Jaxson |date=March 23, 2021 |title=An Immersive Installation Brings the Goodnight Moon Room to Manhattan |url=https://metropolismag.com/projects/good-night-house-fort-makers/ |access-date=2026-04-06 |website=Metropolis |language=en-US}}</ref> drawing, sculpture, poetry, and performance art. Alcalá resides in Los Angeles.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 4, 2021 |title=Meet an Artist Monday: Marcel Alcalá |url=https://www.laweekly.com/meet-an-artist-monday-marcel-alcala/ |access-date=2026-04-06 |website=[[LA Weekly]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Marcel Alcalá was born in 1990, in [[Santa Ana, California]].<ref name="Durón-2022">{{Cite web |last=Durón |first=Maximilíano |date=March 10, 2022 |title=Night Gallery Takes on Marcel Alcalá, L.A.-Based Artist on the Rise |url=https://www.artnews.com/art-news/market/night-gallery-marcel-alcala-1234621619/ |access-date= |website=ARTnews.com |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="Hammer Museum, UCLA-2023">{{Cite web |date=2023-10-24 |title=Marcel Alcalá |url=https://hammer.ucla.edu/made-la-2023-acts-living/marcel-alcala |access-date=2026-02-13 |website=Hammer Museum, UCLA}}</ref> They are [[Xicanx]] (or [[Mexican Americans|Mexican-American]]), and queer.<ref name="Hammer Museum, UCLA-2023" /><ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=November 7, 2017 |title=East LA Artist Marcel Alcalá Is in Full Bloom |url=https://www.intomore.com/culture/east-la-artist-marcel-alcala-is-in-full-bloom/ |access-date=2026-04-07 |website=Into magazine |language=en}}</ref>

Alcalá received a [[BFA degree]] in 2012 from the [[School of the Art Institute of Chicago]]. They were showcased as an artist-in-residence at the [[Skowhegan School of Painting and Sculpture]] (2022) in Maine.<ref name="Hammer Museum, UCLA-2023" /> 

== Career ==
Alcalá began hosting performances in Los Angeles and this became a part of their identity. They incorporated [[Payasa]] (clown) parties and developed this vision of utilizing clowns as a contribution to their art work. These performances were hosted at McDonald's in Los Angeles as well as in Chicago and Europe. Throughout these events Alcalá met various artists and learned about their work. They have worked with poet Emily Lucid to collaborate on writing their first collection of poetry called "Puro Silencio."<ref>{{Cite web |title=Meet Marcel Alcalá |url=https://voyagela.com/interview/meet-marcel-alcala/ |access-date=2026-03-04 |website=VoyageLA}}</ref> 

Alcalá has worked with various mediums such as oil pastels, oil, gouache, and acrylic to create paintings. Their solo exhibition, ''Gallo Gallina'' (2024), was showcased at Marlborough, New York City consists of ten of their new paintings and various watercolor drawings.<ref name="Soboleva">{{Cite web |last=Soboleva |first=Ksenia M. |title=Marcel Alcalá: Gallo Gallina |url=https://brooklynrail.org/event/2024/04/16/marcel-alcala-gallo-gallina/ |access-date=2026-04-07 |website=The Brooklyn Rail |language=en |type=video}}</ref> ''In the Performance of Being'', they primarily showcase oil paintings at the Night Gallery, Los Angeles in 2023.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=MARCEL ALCALÁ - The Performance of Being - Viewing Room - Night Gallery |url=https://www.nightgallery.ca/viewing-room/marcel-alcala2#:~:text=The%20Performance%20of%20Being%20(2023,especially%20meaningful,%20and%20quite%20real.&text=Marcel%20Alcal%C3%A1%20(b.,and%20works%20in%20Los%20Angeles. |access-date=2026-02-13 |website=Night Gallery}}</ref> During 2020 and 2021, Alcalá held another exhibition called ''Solita'', in the same location which consisted of oil paintings, gouache works, and ceramic pieces made during quarantine.<ref name="García-2020">{{Cite web |last=García |first=Beatriz |date=December 15, 2020 |title=Border Art: Marcel Alcalá's 'kink' surrealism |url=https://aldianews.com/en/culture/heritage-and-history/irreverent-and-cross-border |access-date=2026-04-06 |website=Al Día News |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Westall |first=Mark |date=March 11, 2022 |title=Night Gallery now represents Los Angeles-based artist Marcel Alcalá. |url=https://fadmagazine.com/2022/03/11/night-gallery-now-represents-los-angeles-based-artist-marcel-alcala/ |access-date=2026-04-06 |website=FAD Magazine |language=en-GB}}</ref> Another pivotal moment in their career is having the opportunity for their work to be acquired by Cheech Marin since the inauguration of the museum in Riverside named, [[The Cheech Marin Center for Chicano Art & Culture]], known to acquire one of the biggest collections of Chicanx works.<ref name="Curr-2022">{{Cite web |date=September 22, 2022 |title=Latinx Artist Marcel Alcalá Is in The Ascendant |url=https://officemagazine.net/latinx-artist-marcel-alcal%C3%A1-ascendant |access-date=2026-02-13 |website=[[Office Magazine]]|last=Curr|first=Sarah}}</ref>

In a 2022 interview they stated they have written a poetry book, performed as a clown in underground clubs in Los Angeles, and have written a movie script in Brooklyn.<ref name="Curr-2022" />

'''Gil Moreira Lameiras''' (born 7 March 1994) is a Portuguese football [[Manager (association football)|manager]] and former football and [[futsal]] player who played as a [[midfielder]]. He is the current manager of [[Vitória S.C. B|Vitória de Guimarães B]].

==Playing career==
Born in [[Fafe]], Lameiras played for hometown sides [[A.D. Fafe]] and [[Desportivo Ases de São Jorge]] as a youth, before playing as a senior for [[G.D. Travassós]] in the regional leagues. In 2016, he moved to [[Operário F.C. de Antime|OFC Antime]], before returning to his first club Fafe in the following year, but now for their [[futsal]] team.

==Managerial career==
Lameiras began his coaching career in 2017, as an assistant of the under-9 squad of [[Vitória S.C.|Vitória de Guimarães]]. He subsequently worked under the same capacity in the following years, before taking over the under-13 team in 2021.

On 10 July 2023, after being in charge of the under-15s the previous season, Lameiras was appointed manager of the under-17 squad.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://vitoriasc.pt/2023/07/10/gil-lameiras-assume-equipa-de-sub-17/|title=Gil Lameiras é o novo treinador de Sub-17|trans-title=Gil Lameiras is the new under-17 manager|publisher=Vitória SC|language=pt|date=10 July 2023|accessdate=20 April 2026}}</ref> On 25 June of the following year, he was named at the helm of [[Vitória S.C. B|the reserves]] in the [[Campeonato de Portugal (league)|Campeonato de Portugal]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://vitoriasc.pt/2024/06/25/gil-lameiras-assume-comando-tecnico-da-equipa-b/|title=Gil Lameiras assume comando técnico da equipa B|trans-title=Gil Lameiras takes over the technical command of the B-team|publisher=Vitória SC|language=pt|date=25 June 2024|accessdate=20 April 2026}}</ref>

On 15 December 2025, after leading the B-side to a [[2024–25 Campeonato de Portugal|promotion]] to the [[Liga 3 (Portugal)|Liga 3]] and having the side in the second place of that category, Lameiras renewed his contract until 2028.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://vitoriasc.pt/2025/12/15/gil-lameiras-renova-ate-2028/|title=Gil Lameiras renova até 2028|trans-title=Gil Lameiras renews until 2028|publisher=Vitória SC|language=pt|date=15 December 2025|accessdate=20 April 2026}}</ref> The following 9 March, he replaced sacked [[Luís Pinto (footballer, born 1989)|Luís Pinto]] at the helm of the first team in the [[Primeira Liga]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cnnportugal.iol.pt/liga/vitoria-guimaraes/v-guimaraes-gil-lameiras-sobe-da-equipa-b-para-suceder-a-luis-pinto|title=V. Guimarães: Gil Lameiras sobe da equipa B para suceder a Luís Pinto|trans-title=V. '''Ellie Walker''' (born June 12, 1999) is an American professional soccer player who plays as a [[defender (soccer)|defender]] for New Zealand club [[Wellington Phoenix FC (women)|Wellington Phoenix]] of the [[A-League Women]]. She previously played for [[S.C.U. Torreense (women)|Torreense]] and [[S.C. Braga (women)|S.C. Braga]] of the Portuguese [[Campeonato Nacional Feminino]] before joining the Wellington Phoenix in June 2025. Walker played [[college soccer]] for the [[Portland Pilots|University of Portland]].

==Early life==
Walker was born on June 12, 1999, in [[Portland, Oregon]], United States.<ref name='soccerdonna'>{{cite web|url=https://www.soccerdonna.de/en/ellie-walker/profil/spieler_75355.html|title=Ellie Walker - Player profile|website=Soccer Donna|access-date=April 21, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://wellingtonphoenix.com/player/ellie-walker/|title=Ellie Walker|website={{A-League team|WP}}|access-date=April 21, 2026}}</ref> She was born to Robyn and John, with John having played [[college basketball]] for [[Lewis–Clark State College]]. Walker attended [[Columbia River High School]] in [[Vancouver, Washington]].<ref name='portland'>{{cite web|url=https://portlandpilots.com/sports/womens-soccer/roster/ellie-walker/7853|title=Ellie Walker - Women's Soccer|website=[[Portland Pilots]]|access-date=April 21, 2026}}</ref>

==College career==
===University of Portland===
On August 18, 2017, Walker made her debut for the [[Portland Pilots|University of Portland]] in a 2–1 win against [[Portland State Vikings|Portland State]]. Walker scored her first goal for the Pilots in a 1–0 on October 21, 2017, against [[Gonzaga Bulldogs|Gonzaga]]. Across five seasons from 2017 to 2021, Walker made 82 appearances and scored 2 goals. She graduated and majored in [[political science]].<ref name='portland'/>

==Club career==
===Torreense===
In 2022, Walker signed for [[S.C.U. Torreense (women)|Torreense]] of the Portuguese [[Campeonato Nacional Feminino]], where she played two seasons.<ref name='wp'>{{cite web|url=https://wellingtonphoenix.com/news/sporting-braga-defender-joins-the-nix/|title=Sporting Braga defender joins the Nix|date=June 12, 2025|access-date=April 21, 2026|website={{A-League team|WP}}}}</ref> During the [[2022–23 Campeonato Nacional Feminino|2022–23 season]], Walker made 22 appearances in the league and scored 1 goal. Walker's first professional goal came in a 2–2 draw against [[C.S. Marítimo (women)|Marítimo]] on March 19, 2023. She also made 1 appearance in the [[Taça de Portugal Feminina|Taça de Portugal]] and 2 in the [[Taça da Liga Feminina|Taça da Liga]].<ref name='soccerdonna'/>

The [[2023–24 Campeonato Nacional Feminino|following season]] Walker made 22 appearances and scored 2 goals in the league, alongside 2 appearances each in the Taça de Portugal and Taça da Liga.<ref name='soccerdonna'/>

===Braga===
[[S.C. Braga (women)|S.C. Braga]] signed Walker for the [[2024–25 Campeonato Nacional Feminino|2024–25 season]]. She made her debut for the club on September 1, 2024, playing 90 minutes in a 6–1 win against [[F.C. Famalicão (women)|FC Famalicão]]. Walker made 18 league appearances, 4 appearances in the Taça de Portugal, and 2 appearances in the Taça da Liga, scoring one goal in the latter.<ref name='soccerdonna'/> Walker helped the club qualify for the [[UEFA Women's Champions League]] after the club finished in third place.<ref name='wp'/>

Allen briefly appeared in federal court on April 27 for an initial hearing, flanked by US Marshals. Appearing before federal judge Zia Faruqui on May 4, Allen alleged he had been put in [[Physical restraint|five-point restraints]], which prompted Faruqui to remark that Allen was being treated worse than the [[Criminal proceedings in the January 6 United States Capitol attack|January 6 partisans]].{{Cite web |last=Lybrand |first=Holmes |date=May 4, 2026 |title=Judge compares jail treatment of press dinner gunman to US Capitol rioters {{!}} CNN Politics |url=https://www.cnn.com/2026/05/04/politics/cole-allen-gunman-jail-conditions-january-6 |access-date=May 30, 2026 |website=CNN |language=en}} On May 5, Allen was indicted on four charges, which included attempting to assassinate the president. Jiang later announced from the stage that Trump planned to give a briefing from the White House and that the dinner would be rescheduled within 30 days. Sources told CBS News that the suspect had told law enforcement he was trying to shoot officials from the [[Second presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration]].{{Cite news |date=April 26, 2026 |title=Suspect in shooting at White House Correspondents' Dinner identified as 31-year-old California man|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/white-house-correspondents-dinner-shooting-suspect-cole-allen/ |access-date=April 26, 2026 |work=[[CBS News]] |language=en-US |first1=Nicole |last1=Sganga |last2=Jacobs |last3=Milton |first3=Pat |last4=Schecter |first4=Anna |first2=Jennifer |last5=Tanyos |first5=Faris |last6=Czachor |first6=Emily Mae}} The day after the shooting, the Department of Justice announced that "preliminary findings" suggested Trump was the intended target.{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/live/c1je28p42ret?post=asset%3A046439c3-0876-4638-8f7b-348d8bd55b31#post |title=Trump and his officials 'likely' targets of suspected gunman, acting attorney general says |work=[[BBC News]] |date=April 26, 2026}} Other media galas planned for the same night in Washington, D.C., continued unabated including events associated with [[Substack]], [[MS NOW]], and ''[[Time (magazine)|Time]]''.{{cite news |first=Callie |last=Holtermann |title=D.C. media parties go on, despite news of gunfire |url=https://www.nytimes.com/live/2026/04/25/us/trump-correspondents-dinner-shooting/dc-media-parties-go-on-despite-news-of-gunfire |date=April 26, 2026 |work=[[The New York Times]] |access-date=April 26, 2026}} Oz Pearlman, who had been entertaining Trump at the Correspondents' Dinner in the moments before the shooting, arrived at the MS NOW event feeling "shook up" but glad that the parties were going on.
