Washington shooting at Trump event |url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/apr/26/violence-must-never-be-the-way-world-leaders-react-to-washington-shooting-at-trump-event |access-date=April 26, 2026 |work=[[The Guardian]] |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}{{cite web |title=World leaders react to Washington press gala shooting |url=https://www.lemonde.fr/en/international/article/2026/04/26/world-leaders-react-to-washington-press-gala-shooting_6752848_4.html |work=[[Le Monde]] |access-date=April 26, 2026 |date=April 26, 2026|agency=[[Agence France-Presse]]}}{{Cite news |title=World reacts to shooting at White House correspondents' dinner |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/4/26/world-reacts-to-shooting-at-white-house-correspondents-dinner |access-date=April 26, 2026 |work=[[Al Jazeera English|Al Jazeera]] |language=en |date=April 26, 2026 |agency=[[Associated Press]] |archive-date=April 26, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260426152502/https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/4/26/world-reacts-to-shooting-at-white-house-correspondents-dinner |url-status=live }} The condemnation from Ukraine was made by Foreign Minister [[Andrii Sybiha]],{{Cite web |date=April 27, 2026 |title=Ukraine’s MFA condemns shooting during White House Correspondents Dinner |url=https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-polytics/4116785-ukraines-mfa-condemns-shooting-during-white-house-correspondents-dinner.html |access-date=May 2, 2026 |website=www.ukrinform.net |language=en |archive-date=April 28, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260428040430/https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-polytics/4116785-ukraines-mfa-condemns-shooting-during-white-house-correspondents-dinner.html |url-status=live }} and not President [[Volodymyr Zelenskyy]]. This has been interpreted as a sign of the Ukrainian president's growing frustration with the [[United States and the Russian invasion of Ukraine|U.S. approach to the Russia-Ukraine war]] under [[Second presidency of Donald Trump|Trump's presidency]].{{cite news |last1=Zadorozhnyy |first1=Tim |title=How Zelensky ran out of patience with Trump — and what it means for US-Ukraine relations |url=https://kyivindependent.com/ukraine-hits-limits-of-patience-with-trump-as-trust-erodes-behind-the-scenes/ |access-date=May 2, 2026 |work=The Kyiv Independent |date=April 30, 2026 |language=en |archive-date=May 3, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260503101915/https://kyivindependent.com/ukraine-hits-limits-of-patience-with-trump-as-trust-erodes-behind-the-scenes/ |url-status=live }} ==Analysis== ''[[El País]]''{{'}}s correspondent Iker Seisdedos characterized the shooting as "another sign of the increasingly tense atmosphere in the United States". Seisdedos placed the incident in the context of recent political violence in the United States, citing attacks or plots targeting figures including [[Steve Scalise]], [[Gretchen Whitmer]], [[Brett Kavanaugh]], [[Paul Pelosi]], and [[Charlie Kirk]]. [[Luke Broadwater]], White House correspondent for ''[[The New York Times]]'', discussed the shooting in the context of security concerns and recent threats against Trump.{{cite news |last=Broadwater |first=Luke |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/04/26/us/politics/trump-gunman-security-violence.html |title=Again, a Gunman Got Perilously Close to Trump |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=April 26, 2026 |access-date=April 26, 2026}} [[David Smith (journalist)|David Smith]], the Washington bureau chief for ''[[The Guardian]]'', wrote that the incident reflected the prevalence of political violence in the United States{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/apr/26/white-house-correspondents-dinner-shooting-covering-trump |title=I've covered Trump for a decade. At the White House correspondents' dinner, darkness came viscerally close |work=[[The Guardian]] |last=Smith |first=David |date=April 26, 2026 |publication-place=Washington |access-date=April 26, 2026}} and noted that Trump himself had been criticized in the past for violent suggestions, such as purging the US of crime on "one really violent day".{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/apr/26/white-house-correspondents-dinner-shooting-washington-dc|title=Washington in shock after White House press dinner shooting: 'an angry, polarized nation'|work=The Guardian|last=Smith|first=David|date=April 26, 2026|access-date=April 26, 2026}} After the shooting, Aaron Blake of [[CNN]] wrote about an emerging split reality in the US, explaining how the reaction to recent acts of political violence reflected increasingly warped views of the perpetrators from people from both the left and the right, as well as how both sides were overwhelmingly likely to blame the other for those acts.{{cite news |url=https://www.cnn.com/2026/04/27/politics/trump-violent-rhetoric-analysis |title=Trump's hypocritical crusade on violent rhetoric — and the country's emerging split reality |work=[[CNN]] |last=Blake |first=Aaron |date=April 27, 2026 |access-date=April 27, 2026}} ==Misinformation and conspiracy theories== {{See also|Conspiracy theories in United States politics}} Media and fact checkers reported that [[conspiracy theories]] and unsupported claims rapidly circulated following the shooting at the Correspondents' Dinner.{{cite magazine |url=https://www.wired.com/story/staged-conspiracy-theories-are-everywhere-following-white-house-correspondents-dinner-shooting/ |url-access=limited |title='STAGED': Conspiracy Theories Are Everywhere Following White House Correspondents' Dinner Shooting |first=David |last=Gilbert |publication-date=April 26, 2026 |magazine=[[Wired (magazine)|Wired]] |access-date=April 26, 2026 |quote=In the immediate aftermath of the attack on the White House Correspondents' Dinner on Saturday night, influencers, pundits, and random posters lit up social media platforms like X, Bluesky, and Instagram with conspiracy theories about the attack and the alleged shooter.
Both left and right-wing accounts claimed, without evidence, that the attack was staged. }}{{cite web |url=https://www.politifact.com/article/2026/apr/26/Trump-White-House-correspondents-dinner-conspiracy/ |title=Fact-checking falsehoods after shooting in hotel hosting correspondents' dinner Trump attended |last=Sherman |publication-date=April 26, 2026 |website=[[PolitiFact]] |access-date=April 26, 2026 |quote=[Contents:] Karoline Leavitt's remarks about "shots fired" referred to Trump's planned speech / Suspect was tackled, not shot / Fox News reporter's clipped call isn't evidence the shooting was staged / Man holding up a card was an entertainer, not signaling a shooting. |date=April 26, 2026|first=Amy}} This surge of conspiracy theories was described and commented on by national{{cite web |url=https://www.ap.org/news-highlights/elections/2026/reporters-covered-the-correspondents-dinner-shooting-in-real-time-conspiracy-theories-still-spread/ |title=Reporters covered the correspondents’ dinner shooting in real time. Conspiracy theories still spread |author=Melissa Goldin |publication-date=April 27, 2026 |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=May 1, 2026 |quote=(...) [[Jen Golbeck]], a professor at the University of Maryland who studies conspiracy theories, said a lack of trust in institutions and an inability to sort fact from fiction create a "textbook recipe" for such rumors. But, she said, even when an abundance of information is available the entertainment value of conspiracy theories can still prevail. (...) Emily Vraga, a professor at the University of Minnesota who studies political misinformation, said that sometimes more information is not necessarily better, especially in such a polarized time when people can pick and choose the facts they like and assemble their own narrative puzzles. (...) }}{{cite web |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/media/5851732-conspiracy-theories-trump-whca-dinner/ |title=Trump assassination attempt sparks new wave of unfounded conspiracy theories |author=Dominick Mastrangelo |publication-date=April 27, 2026 |publisher=[[The Hill (newspaper)|The Hill]] |access-date=May 1, 2026 |quote=(...) "We’re in an information environment where people are just not believing anything they see because they’ve become so exhausted by the steady tide of information everyone is sharing that later turns out to be not true," Katie Sanders, editor in chief of the fact checking website PolitiFact, told The Hill. "People might want to tune all of it out, but that means they’re not in a good position to separate what’s true when breaking news happens." (...) "Shootings or reports of shootings are chaotic environments, and the chaos is what attracts the conspiratorial thinker," said Geoff Dancy, a political scientist at the University of Toronto. "People who seek out conspiracies are often looking for comfort or order among disorder. It could be a comforting thought to think this is all planned. It sort of allays your fears to think this isn’t just some person who had access to weapons and snapped … that’s scary." }}{{cite podcast |host=[[Scott Detrow]], Molly Olmstead |date=April 27, 2026 |title=Correspondents dinner shooting unleashes conspiracy theories |url=https://www.npr.org/2026/04/27/nx-s1-5801423/correspondents-dinner-shooting-unleashes-conspiracy-theories |work=[[Consider This (podcast)|Consider This]] |publisher=[[NPR]] |time=2:28 min. |access-date=May 1, 2026 |quote=[Molly Olmstead, staff writer with Slate:] (...) I don't see any way for it to get better. It just seems that this is the America we live in now. This is the reality we live in now. It seems to me that for the foreseeable future, the different political factions are going to be operating not just on different views but entirely different realities. (...) [Total running time, 8:31 min.] |archive-date=April 28, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260428205413/https://www.npr.org/2026/04/27/nx-s1-5801423/correspondents-dinner-shooting-unleashes-conspiracy-theories |url-status=live }} and international media,{{cite web |url=https://www.barrons.com/news/trump-shooting-scare-renews-staged-conspiracy-theory-8f19df5d |title=Trump Shooting Scare Renews 'Staged' Conspiracy Theory |author=Anuj Chopra |publication-date=April 27, 2026 |publisher=[[Barron's]] |access-date=May 1, 2026 |quote=[From Agence France-Presse/AFP News ] (...) The trend underscores how Americans on both sides of the political divide are prone to outlandish conspiracy theories, as many turn to partisan influencers for information amid mistrust of mainstream media, researchers say. (...) |archive-date=April 28, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260428221633/https://www.barrons.com/news/trump-shooting-scare-renews-staged-conspiracy-theory-8f19df5d |url-status=live }}{{cite web |url=https://www.euronews.com/my-europe/2026/04/29/conspiracy-theories-abound-after-white-house-correspondents-dinner-shooting |title=Conspiracy theories abound after White House Correspondents' Dinner shooting |author=James Thomas, Tamsin Paternoster |publication-date=April 29, 2026 |publisher=[[Euronews]] |access-date=May 1, 2026 |quote=(...) In the aftermath of the incident, influencers and social media users flooded X, Bluesky and Instagram with allegations that the attack was staged, despite multiple journalists reporting first-hand on the incident. (...) [Includes video. Total running time, 1:56 min.] |archive-date=April 30, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260430071622/https://www.euronews.com/my-europe/2026/04/29/conspiracy-theories-abound-after-white-house-correspondents-dinner-shooting |url-status=live }}{{cite AV media |people=[[David Common]], Carmen Celestini |date=April 30, 2026 |title=Conspiracy theories flood internet after White House correspondents' dinner shooting |medium=Internet video |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8KRoBa8Y8U0 |access-date=May 1, 2026 |time=0:24 min. |publisher=[[CBC News]] |quote=[Video description:] On social media — and across the political spectrum — conspiracies theories are spreading about the shooting at the White House correspondents' dinner. Carmen Celestini, who studies disinformation, extremism and conspiracy theories at the University of Waterloo, says it's a symptom of low trust in institutions. |archive-date=April 30, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260430155726/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8KRoBa8Y8U0 |url-status=live }} often attributing it to distrust in the institutions (the government, the media themselves) and mutual distrust by both sides of the political spectrum. [[Donie O'Sullivan (journalist)|Donie O'Sullivan]] discussed how prominent former Trump's supporters like [[Tucker Carlson]] and [[Marjorie Taylor Greene]] have recently questioned the official narrative on the [[attempted assassination of Donald Trump in Pennsylvania]], and quotes [[Keith Olbermann]] and [[Cenk Uygur]] blaming Trump's and his administration's [[False or misleading statements by Donald Trump|mendacity]] for their own mistrust of their statements.{{cite news |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2026/04/27/politics/conspiracy-theories-whcd-attack |title=Facts compete with conspiracy theories after WHCD attack |first=Donie |last=O'Sullivan |publication-date=April 27, 2026 |work=[[CNN]] |access-date=April 27, 2026 |quote=Some of the best-known journalists in the country were gathered in the Hilton ballroom on Saturday night and immediately got to work establishing the facts of what had happened. But immediately — before anything was known about the suspect and his motives — the word 'staged' started to emerge as a trend across social media platforms. ... [The article also describes and debunks the claims that circulated about Karoline Leavitt and Aishah Hasnie.] }} [[NBC News]] described and analyzed the fast spread of misinformation, stating that "Conspiracy theories and a knee-jerk skepticism of current events have become the default response for a growing number of Americans, deepened by the loss of trust in institutions and supercharged by starkly partisan politics."{{cite news |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/tech/misinformation/conspiracy-theories-staged-white-house-correspondents-dinner-rcna342212 |title=False flag conspiracy theories swirl around White House Correspondents' Dinner attack. Baseless claims that the incident was staged swirled almost immediately. By the next day, the idea had spread across social media. Even Trump noted the speed |first1=Jason |last1=Abbruzzese |first2=Gibran Caroline |last2=Boyce |first3=Julie |last3=Tsirkin |date=April 27, 2026 |work=[[NBC News]] |access-date=April 27, 2026 |quote=Even as the events were unfolding, some had already anticipated the reaction. 'You know right-wing media is filled with all kinds of conspiracy theories lately about how President Trump's first assassination attempt was phony and fake?' Rep. [[Jamie Raskin]], D-Md., told NBC News as he left the dinner. 'This is going to fuel all of that stuff, I'm sure.'}} White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt called the conspiracy theories "crazy nonsense";{{cite AV media |people=Aishah Hasnie, Karoline Leavitt |date=April 27, 2026 |title=White House says conspiracy theories about shooting are 'crazy nonsense' |medium=Internet video |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/video/white-house-says-conspiracy-theories-about-shooting-are-crazy-nonsense-262180933722 |access-date=April 27, 2026 |publisher=[[NBC News]] |quote=[Video description:] White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt was asked about how the administration plans to combat the conspiracy theories about the White House Correspondents' Association dinner shooting from spreading. Leavitt dismissed the rumors as "crazy nonsense" and planned to dispel any misinformation by assuring transparency. [Total running time, 1:15 min.]}} Trump called them "sick".{{cite AV media |people=Mark Owen, Vedika Bahl, Donald Trump |date=April 27, 2026 |title='Staged': Conspiracy theories surge after shooting at White House Correspondents' Dinner |medium=Internet video |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cEwqADrmxEc |access-date=April 27, 2026 |time=1:38 min. |publisher=[[France 24]] |quote=[Includes an excerpt of April 27 Trump's CBS interview, in which he discusses the conspiracy theories about the shooting. Total running time, 5:11 min.]}} ==="Staged" allegations=== One of the main reported false narratives was claims that the entire event was faked for political gain. On [[Bluesky]], many users posted "STAGED", [[Attempted assassination of Donald Trump in Pennsylvania#Misinformation and conspiracy theories|echoing the response]] to the Trump assassination attempt in Butler, Pennsylvania, in 2024, whereas on [[X (social network)|X]], others claimed that the shooting was staged to increase support for Trump's plan to build a new [[White House State Ballroom|ballroom in the White House]].{{cite news |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/business/2026/04/27/whcd-shooting-conspiracy-theories-trump/ |title=First came the shooting. Then, the conspiracy theories. The shooting at the White House correspondents' dinner has sparked conspiracy theories on the left and the right that it was staged to drum up support for Trump and his ballroom |first=Liam |last=Scott |publication-date=April 27, 2026 |work=[[The Washington Post]] |access-date=April 27, 2026 |quote=The theory has bounded the political spectrum, from the pro-Trump right to staunch critics of the president, such as [[Jasmine Crockett|Crockett]]. ... About a fifth of the left-wing and liberal influencers and politicians who posted about the shooting used conspiratorial language, according to a ''Post'' analysis of social media posts and podcasts. ... Some, like former MAGA influencer [[Ashley St. Clair]], have pointed to other moments in the aftermath of the shooting to suggest a different kind of coordination. After dozens of conservative influencers and Trump supporters made similar posts on X saying the incident showed the need for a new White House ballroom, as Trump has requested, St. Clair argued that many of them had probably shared the talking point in private groups, so as to boost its appeal. 'Everything in MAGA is fake, staged and coordinated,' she said in a TikTok video.}} Other reasons given for staging the shooting were Trump's [[Opinion polling on the second Trump presidency|low approval ratings]], and his actions in the [[2026 Iran war]].{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/04/26/technology/white-house-correspondents-dinner-shooting-conspiracy-theories.html |url-access=subscription |title=Rumors and Speculation Swirl Online After Shooting at Washington Dinner |first1=Stuart A. |last1=Thompson |first2=Tiffany |last2=Hsu |first3=Steven Lee |last3=Myers |publication-date=April 26, 2026 |work=[[The New York Times]] |access-date=April 27, 2026 |quote=This time, users from across the political spectrum were participating in the chaos on platforms like X, Facebook and TikTok. Some users claimed that the attack was 'staged,' suggesting without evidence that it was part of an apparent plot by Mr. Trump or others to distract from bad polling numbers or the war with Iran. The term 'staged' surged to more than 300,000 posts on X by midday Sunday, according to data by TweetBinder, a social media analytics company owned by Audiense. (At least some of those posts refuted the notion that the attack was planned.)}} Comments from Leavitt and her husband Nicholas Riccio in particular were seen as them having prior knowledge of the shooting: Leavitt told [[Fox News]] shortly before "There will be some shots fired tonight in the room" in apparent reference to a planned speech of Trump.{{cite news |last1=Esposito |first1=Laura |title=Karoline Leavitt Made Bizarre 'Shots Fired' Brag Minutes Before Shooting |url=https://www.thedailybeast.com/karoline-leavitt-made-bizarre-shots-fired-brag-minutes-before-shooting/ |access-date=April 27, 2026 |work=[[The Daily Beast]] |date=April 26, 2026 |language=en}}{{cite news |last1=Tolliver |first1=Jazmin |title=Karoline Leavitt's Eerily Prescient Words Go Viral After Correspondents' Dinner Shooting |url=https://www.huffpost.com/entry/karoline-leavitt-shots-fired-white-house-correspondents-dinner_n_69ee55dce4b0d1d8ce94cd5b |access-date=April 27, 2026 |work=[[HuffPost]] |date=April 26, 2026 |language=en}} ''[[Snopes]]'' notes that in English "[t]he phrase '[[wikt:shots fired|shots fired]]' is a common figure of speech that refers to someone making jokes or jabs at another person. There was no evidence that Leavitt's comment referenced the shooting before it happened."{{cite web|last=Loe|first=Megan|url=https://www.snopes.com/fact-check/karoline-leavitt-shots-fired/|title=Did Leavitt say there would be 'shots fired' before White House correspondents' dinner shooting?|work=[[Snopes]]|date=April 26, 2026|accessdate=April 29, 2026|archive-date=April 29, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260429112741/https://www.snopes.com//fact-check/karoline-leavitt-shots-fired/|url-status=live}} Fox correspondent Aishah Hasnie reported that Riccio emphasized she "need[ed] to be very safe" at the event; while recounting this to the network, Hasnie's call cut out, causing speculation that Fox News was suppressing her account. Hasnie cited poor [[Mobile phone signal|cell reception]] for the call dropping and clarified: "To finish the story, he was telling me to be careful with my own safety because the world is crazy."{{cite news |last1=Sanyal |first1=Shounak |title=Mysterious call drop as Fox News reporter recounts warning by Karoline Leavitt's husband |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/world/us-news/story/white-house-correspondents-dnner-shooting-fox-news-reporter-aishah-hasnie-warning-nicholas-riccio-karoline-leavitt-husband-2902326-2026-04-27 |access-date=April 27, 2026 |work=[[India Today]] |date=April 27, 2026 |language=en}} Social media users claimed that a picture allegedly showing Trump standing behind a curtain observing the commotion at the ballroom proved that the shooting had been staged; that claim was shared in posts that reached millions of users of [[Bluesky]], [[Facebook]], [[Instagram]], [[Threads (social network)|Threads]], [[TikTok]], and [[X (social network)|X]]. ''[[Snopes]]'' reported that even if the photo is authentic, the man in it is not Trump.{{cite web |url=https://www.snopes.com/fact-check/trump-behind-curtain-shooting/ |title=Does photo show Trump standing behind curtain after White House correspondents' dinner shooting? |author=Jordan Liles |publication-date=April 30, 2026 |publisher=Snopes |access-date=May 1, 2026 |quote=(...) However, the image showed another man — not Trump — as revealed in a video recorded in the same moments by Pancho Bernasconi, Getty Images' vice president of global news. (...) |archive-date=May 2, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260502172145/https://www.snopes.com/fact-check/trump-behind-curtain-shooting/ |url-status=live }} ===False information about the suspect=== An X user named True Promise claimed that information gleaned from [[Google Trends]] indicated that the suspect's name had been searched hundreds of times in Israel a day before the incident. According to the ''[[Free Press Journal]]'', this idea was debunked. Another widely spread social media post asserted that he had been seen wearing a sweatshirt associated with the [[Israel Defense Force]], but this claim could not be independently confirmed.{{cite web |url=https://www.freepressjournal.in/world/was-shooting-staged-viral-posts-claim-name-of-accused-was-searched-hundreds-of-times-in-israel-before-incident |title=Was Trump Shooting Staged? Viral Posts Claim Name Of Accused Was Searched Hundreds Of Times In Israel Before Incident |author=Mishra |publication-date=April 26, 2025 |work=[[The Free Press Journal]] |access-date=April 26, 2026 |quote=However, verification efforts found that the suspect's name began trending in Israel only after the shooting took place, contradicting the claim. ... Another viral post alleged that the suspect was seen wearing a sweatshirt associated with the Israel Defense Forces. This claim, however, could not be independently verified. |date=April 26, 2026 |first=Vinay}}{{cite AV media |date=April 26, 2026 |title=White House Dinner Shooter Cole Allen In 'IDF Sweatshirt'? Viral Photo Fuels Israel Speculation |medium=Internet video |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/videos/international/white-house-dinner-shooter-cole-allen-in-idf-sweatshirt-viral-photo-fuels-israel-speculation/videoshow/130534261.cms |access-date=April 26, 2026 |publisher=[[The Times of India]] |quote=[The video describes how the rumors about the suspect's connection to Israel (and him being a Democrat assassin according to [[Laura Loomer]]) were spread, debunking them. Total running time: 7:14 min.] }}{{cite web |url=https://www.snopes.com/articles/473060/cole-allen-idf-sweatshirt/ |title=Does image show White House correspondents' dinner shooting suspect wearing IDF sweatshirt? What we know |author=Emery Winter |publication-date=April 26, 2026 |publisher=[[Snopes]] |access-date=May 1, 2026 |quote=(...) There was no primary source evidence confirming the veracity of the image, and Snopes could not find credible evidence of an Instagram account directly linked to Allen. A LinkedIn account that appeared to be Allen's did not post the image purported to be from his Instagram account.
While not definitive enough to conclusively rate the image's veracity, some details within the image suggested someone generated it using artificial intelligence tools. (...) |archive-date=April 29, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260429112744/https://www.snopes.com//articles/473060/cole-allen-idf-sweatshirt/ |url-status=live }} A viral image of a passport belonging to an [[India]]n woman, who was supposedly married to the suspect, was in fact an [[Generative AI|AI-generated]] forgery.{{cite news |last1=Biswas |first1=Shuvrajit Das |title=Cole Tomas Allen: Fact-checking claims about White House correspondents' dinner shooting suspect's wife and marriage |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-news/us-news/cole-tomas-allen-married-fact-check-claims-about-wife-white-house-correspondents-dinner-shooting-suspect-motive-details-101777237413313.html |access-date=April 27, 2026 |work=[[Hindustan Times]] |date=April 27, 2026 |language=en}} ==See also== * [[2026 in Washington, D.C.]] ==Notes== {{notelist}} ==References== {{Reflist}} == External ==Club career==

Hayashi plays as a [[midfielder]]. Australian newspaper ''[[Nichigo Press]]'' wrote in 2023 that "even though she is not particularly tall, she is able to play physically in a league that demands strength because of her low center of gravity that makes her strong enough not to be outmuscled, and her skill in reading the flow of the opponent's attack. Her versatility, as she can play in more attacking positions when needed, is also one of her strengths".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://nichigopress.jp/topics-item/68351/|title=不動／日豪フットボール新時代 第135回|trans-title=Fudo / A New Era of Japan-Australia Football, Part 135|language=ja|publisher=[[Nichigo Press]]|date=28 July 2023|access-date=27 April 2026}}</ref>

'''Madison Marilla''' (born September 22, 1997)<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |last=Njuguna |first=Ciku |date=2026-04-24 |title=Madison Marilla was told she'd never go to a mainstream school — then she became a teacher - Legit.ng |url=https://www.legit.ng/ask-legit/biographies/1706002-madison-marilla-told-d-a-mainstream-school-a-teacher/ |access-date=2026-05-05 |website=www.legit.ng |language=en}}</ref> is an American [[autistic]] television personality, social media [[Content creation|content creator]] and former [[elementary school]] special education student activities director.<ref name=":6" /><ref name=":2" /><ref name=":7">{{Cite web |last=Allard |first=Bethany |date=2025-07-08 |title=Madison Marilla of 'Love on the Spectrum' talks jewelry, Disneyland, and creating content |url=https://mashable.com/article/madison-marilla-love-on-the-spectrum-in-my-bag |access-date=2026-04-29 |website=Mashable |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/shorts/zQIIICUbM0I |title=I love talking about teaching. I answered a lot of my subscribers’ questions in my recent VLOG |language=en |access-date=2026-09-17 |via=www.youtube.com}}</ref> 

She is best known for appearing on seasons 3 and 4 of [[Netflix]]'s [[Love on the Spectrum (American TV series)|''Love on the Spectrum'']].<ref name=":6">{{Cite web |title=Netflix helped a Tampa Bay woman find ‘Love on the Spectrum.’ What’s next? |url=https://www.tampabay.com/life-culture/2025/05/09/netflix-love-on-spectrum-reality-show-tampa-st-petersburg/ |access-date=2026-04-29 |website=Tampa Bay Times |language=en}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Madison Marilla was born on September 22, 1997<ref name=":3" /> in [[North Carolina]]. She is the daughter of Jenny Marilla and Brennan Marilla. She also has one younger brother.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Robinette |first=Ashlyn |date=2026-04-22 |title=Madison Marilla's Dad Shares the 'Sweet' Moment Love on the Spectrum's Tyler White Asked for His Blessing to Propose |url=https://people.com/madison-marilla-dad-shares-the-sweet-moment-love-on-the-spectrum-star-tyler-white-asked-for-his-blessing-to-propose-11956240 |access-date=2026-04-29 |website=People}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q7v1hUp52v4 |title=Madison Marilla: Embracing Every Part of Me |date=2026-04-22 |last=The Squeeze |access-date=2026-04-29 |via=YouTube}}</ref> Marilla and her family moved to [[Santa Rosa, California]] after her father got a job there. She repeated the eighth grade after moving to [[Massachusetts]].<ref name=":0" />

Marilla was diagnosed with autism at age 2.<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.facebook.com/reel/294772485485908/ |title=Ms. Madison Marilla's Journey |date=2021-04-16 |last=Plymouth Public Schools |type=Video |language=en |time=0:09 |access-date=2026-05-03 |via=Facebook}}</ref> Doctors told Marilla's parents she would never be able to speak or attend a [[Mainstreaming (education)|mainstream]] school. Marilla was subsequently enrolled in [[speech therapy]], [[occupational therapy]], [[applied behavior analysis]] (ABA), and [[social skills training]].<ref name=":5">{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.facebook.com/reel/294772485485908/ |title=Ms. Madison Marilla's Journey |date=2021-04-16 |last=Plymouth Public Schools |type=Video |language=en |time=0:33 |access-date=2026-05-03 |via=Facebook}}</ref> Marilla spoke for the first time at age 4.<ref name=":5" /> She was diagnosed at age 6 with [[Obsessive–compulsive disorder|OCD]], [[Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder|ADHD]] and [[generalized anxiety disorder]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Meet Madison M. |url=https://www.autismspeaks.org/profile/meet-madison-m |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250403132455/https://www.autismspeaks.org/profile/meet-madison-m |archive-date=2025-04-03 |access-date=2026-04-29 |website=[[Autism Speaks]] |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":2" />

In high school, Marilla created an autism awareness club.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Feldberg |first=Isaac |title=L-S student raises autism awareness |url=https://www.wickedlocal.com/story/sudbury-town-crier/2014/04/10/l-s-student-raises-autism/37676028007/ |date=2014-04-10 |access-date=2026-04-30 |website=Wicked Local |language=en-US}}</ref>

Marilla graduated from [[Western New England University]] in 2020 with a [[Bachelor of Arts]] in psychology; she also minored in art. Her studies were largely focused on [[special education]] and ABA.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=A Sparkling Path |url=https://magazine.wne.edu/2025-winter/04-a-sparkling-path-madison-marilla.cfm |access-date=2026-04-29 |website=magazine.wne.edu|publisher=[[Western New England University]]|date=Winter 2025|last=Larsen|first=Emily Mead}}</ref>

== Career ==
In high school, a mentor inspired Marilla to also become a mentor to autistic kids. She later became a mentor for autistic children in school and home-based settings, as well as a social skills group instructor at an after-school and weekend program.<ref name=":1" />

After graduating from college, she worked at several elementary schools in Massachusetts in various special education roles, including as a student activities director.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Harbert |first=Rich |title=Autistic activities director at Plymouth elementary school shows positive side of disorder |url=https://www.wickedlocal.com/story/old-colony-memorial/2021/04/15/plymouth-educator-autism-leads-example/7183706002/ |date=2021-04-15 |access-date=2026-04-30 |website=Wicked Local |language=en-US}}</ref>

Prior to appearing on ''Love on the Spectrum'', she was a big fan of the show, having watched the first two seasons of the American version, as well as the original [[Love on the Spectrum (Australian TV series)|Australian version]]. Ahead of season 2, while Marilla was living in Massachusetts, the show reached out to a life program she was a part of, about her appearing on the show. However she felt the timing wasn't right. She was reached out to a year later and then became a cast member on the show beginning in season 3.<ref name=":0" />

== Personal life ==
As of April 2026, Marilla is engaged to Tyler White, whom she met while appearing on ''Love on the Spectrum.''<ref>{{Cite web |last=Franklin |first=McKinley |date=2026-04-28 |title=‘Love on the Spectrum’ Stars Madison and Tyler Dish on If Their Wedding Will Be Filmed for Netflix Show |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-features/madison-tyler-love-on-the-spectrum-wedding-season-5-1236579358/ |access-date=2026-04-29 |website=The Hollywood Reporter |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Houlis |first=AnnaMarie |date=2026-04-02 |title=Madison Marilla and Tyler White of 'Love on the Spectrum' Are Officially Engaged |url=https://parade.com/news/madison-marilla-tyler-white-love-on-the-spectrum-officially-engaged |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260403081733/https://parade.com/news/madison-marilla-tyler-white-love-on-the-spectrum-officially-engaged |archive-date=2026-04-03 |access-date=2026-04-29 |work=Parade |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-04-02 |title='Love on the Spectrum' Couple Madison Marilla and Tyler White Just Got Engaged |url=https://www.today.com/popculture/tv/love-spectrum-couple-madison-tyler-share-wedding-plans-rcna266364 |access-date=2026-04-29 |website=TODAY.com |language=en}}</ref>

Marilla also makes bracelets and sells them under the brand Madizen, which she started with her older brother when she was 14.<ref name=":7" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":4">{{Cite web |date=2025-04-02 |title=This ‘Love On The Spectrum’ Star Has A Meaningful Career |url=https://www.bustle.com/entertainment/madison-marilla-love-on-the-spectrum-instagram-family-job |access-date=2026-04-29 |website=Bustle |language=en}}</ref>

'''Ellen Brönmark Åkesson''' (born 20 March 1999) is a Swedish [[powerlifter]], [[arm wrestler]], and [[professional wrestler]]. She has been described as "Sweden's strongest woman".<ref name="SkånskaDagbladet2"/><ref name="Sydsvenskan"/><ref name="Corren5"/>

== Powerlifting career ==
Åkesson developed an interest in powerlifting at the age of 17 upon being [[Conscription in Sweden|drafted for military service]] and performing well in an IsoKai isokinetic lift test. She began training at a gym in Skurup.<ref name="SkånskaDagbladet2"/><ref name="Sydsvenskan"/> She began competing in powerlifting contests in 2021.<ref name="Powerlifting"/> That November, she became the Swedish junior champion in powerlifting, lifting a total of 400 kilograms across [[bench press]], [[deadlift]], and [[Squat (exercise)|squat]].<ref name="YstadsAllehanda5"/>

In February 2023, Åkesson competed at the Swedish Championships in [[Skövde]] in the 63 kilogram weight class, winning gold medals for bench press (lifting 97.5 kilograms) and for classic powerlifting (lifting a total of 425 kilograms across the three lifts).<ref name="Corren2"/><ref name="YstadsAllehanda7"/><ref name="Skurupsposten"/><ref name="Corren6"/> In March 2023, Åkesson placed second in the European Classic University Powerlifting Cup in [[Albi]], France, setting [[European University Sports Association]] records in the 63 kilogram weight class for deadlifting (190 kilograms) and bench press (100 kilograms).<ref name="Powerlifting"/><ref name="EuroPowerlifting"/> In October 2023, Åkesson competed in the World University Powerlifting Cup in [[Kranjska Gora]], Slovenia, placing second in the 69 kilogram weight class.<ref name="Goodlift"/>

In July 2024, Åkesson won the 63 kilogram contest at the [[International University Sports Federation]] World University Powerlifting Championships in [[Tartu]], Estonia, lifting a total of 440.5 kilograms across the three lifts.<ref name="Powerlifting"/><ref name="Goodlift"/><ref name="Fisu"/><ref name="Sverigesradio"/> In September 2024, she won the 63 kilogram contest at the XV Western European Powerlifting Championships in [[St. Paul's Bay]], Malta, lifting a total of 460 kilograms across the three lifts.<ref name="Powerlifting"/><ref name="Goodlift"/>

In February 2025, Åkesson won a gold medal at the Swedish championships in [[Borås]] in the 69 kilogram weight class, lifting a total of 490 kilograms across the three lifts.<ref name="YstadsAllehanda3"/><ref name="Corren5"/><ref name="YstadsAllehanda4"/><ref name="SVT"/> During she contest, she set her records for deadlifting (212.5 kilograms) and squat (162.5 kilograms).<ref name="Powerlifting"/><ref name="Räty"/> That same year, she placed fifth in the European Bench Press Championships in [[Valletta]], Malta,<ref name="Powerlifting"/> sixth in the [[International Powerlifting Federation]] World Classic & Equipped Bench Press Championships in [[Drammen]], Norway,<ref name="Goodlift"/> and fifteenth in the European Powerlifting Federation's European Open Classic Powerlifting Championships in [[Malaga]], Spain,<ref name="Goodlift"/> all in the 69 kilogram weight class. The Swedish strength sports magazine ''MAXstyrka'' named Åkesson its Female Athlete of the Year for 2025.<ref name="YstadsAllehanda10"/>

== Arm wrestling career ==
In March 2024, Åkesson competed in arm wrestling at the Swedish Championships in [[Luleå]], winning a silver medal.<ref name="Aftonbladet"/><ref name="YstadsAllehanda13"/> In September–October 2024, she competed in the International Federation of Armwrestling (IFA) World Armwrestling Championships in [[Loutraki]], Greece in the 63 kilogram division, placing second in both the left and right contests.<ref name="Corren4"/><ref name="Arm"/>

In February 2025, Åkesson won gold medals at the Swedish championships in [[Borås]] in both the left and right contests; the arm wrestling contest began at the same time as the powerlifting contest, forcing Åkesson to rush between the two contests.<ref name="YstadsAllehanda3"/><ref name="YstadsAllehanda4"/><ref name="SVT"/><ref name="Corren7"/> In May 2025, she competed in the IFA European Armwrestling Championships in [[Pärnu]], Estonia in the 70 kilogram division, placing third in the right contest and fourth in the left contest.<ref name="Arm2025A"/><ref name="Arm2025B"/> In October–November that year, she competed in the IFA World Armwrestling Championships in [[Baku]], Azerbaijan in the 70 kilogram division, winning both the right and left contests.<ref name="Arm"/><ref name="YstadsAllehanda1"/> In December 2025, she defeated veteran arm wrestler Petra Damm in a contest at the "Clash of Arms" festival in [[Solnahallen]].<ref name="YstadsAllehanda2"/><ref name="YstadsAllehanda11"/>

== Professional wrestling career ==
In August 2025, Åkesson attended a try-out with the American [[professional wrestling promotion]] [[WWE]] in [[New Jersey]] in the United States during its [[SummerSlam (2025)|SummerSlam]] pay-per-view.<ref name="Lambert"/><ref name="Carey2"/> In March 2026, WWE announced that it had signed Åkesson to a contract and assigned her to the [[WWE Performance Center]] in [[Orlando, Florida]] in the United States.<ref name="YstadsAllehanda9"/><ref name="Lambert2"/><ref name="Carey"/><ref name="YstadsAllehanda17"/> She made her first appearance for WWE at the July 28, 2026 ''[[WWE NXT]]'' tapings, giving a [[promo (professional wrestling)|promo]].<ref name="Dubey"/> On September 4, Åkesson was released from WWE without wrestling in an official match.<ref name="Lambert3"/>

'''Dan Lie''' (they/them) is a trans-nonbinary [[Berlin]]-based artist known for their site and time specific environmental sculptures.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Garcia |first=Cynthia |date=2018-02-20 |title=The Art of Life and Death: A conversation with Daniel Lie about his monumental sculpture at Casa Triangulo {{!}} Newcity Brazil |url=https://www.newcitybrazil.com/2018/02/20/the-art-of-life-and-death-a-conversation-with-daniel-lie-about-his-monumental-sculpture-at-casa-triangulo/ |access-date=2026-05-10 |website=www.newcitybrazil.com |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>https://liedaniel.hotglue.me/?BIO</ref> They exhibited as part of the [[61st Venice Biennale|2026 Venice Biennale]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-05-27 |title=Biennale Arte 2026 {{!}} Biennale Arte 2026: the invited artists |url=https://www.labiennale.org/en/news/biennale-arte-2026-invited-artists |access-date=2026-05-10 |website=La Biennale di Venezia |language=en}}</ref>
 
== Career ==
Lie draws from their diasporic heritage and queer identity to create installations that are as much living environments as they are contemplative spaces.<ref>https://tba21.org/artist/Dan_Lie</ref> Since Lie uses organic materials, decay and decomposition becomes part of the installation and makes it difficult to collect.<ref name=":1" />

== Personal life ==
Lie’s mother is from [[Garanhuns]] in [[Pernambuco]] state of [[Brazil]] and their father is from [[Semarang]], in [[Java|Java Island]] of [[Indonesia]].<ref name=":0" /> Lie uses they/them pronouns.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Lloyd-Smith |first=Harriet |date=2019-06-01 |title=Daniel Lie ignites the senses at Jupiter Artland |url=https://www.wallpaper.com/art/daniel-lie-the-negative-years-jupiter-artland |access-date=2026-05-10 |website=Wallpaper* |language=en}}</ref>

Lie has exhibited their organic work in England, Hungary, Indonesia, Germany, Brazil, Chile, in Austria in the 2017 Vienna Festwochen,<ref name=":0" /> and Italy as part of the 2026 Venice Biennale.

'''Analí Márquez Huanca''' (born 10 October 1988) is a Peruvian lawyer and politician. She is the first-vice president and a member of the [[Chamber of Deputies of Peru]] for [[Department of Cusco|Cusco]] and a candidate for [[First Vice President of Peru|first-vice president]] in the [[2026 Peruvian general election]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.eldestapeweb.com/internacionales/elecciones-peru-quien-anali-marquez-vice-roberto-sanchez-202664155922|newspaper=[[El Destape]]|language=Spanish|title=Elecciones en Perú: Analí Márquez, la abogada y dirigente de Cusco que acompaña en la fórmula a Roberto Sánchez|date=4 June 2026|trans-title=Elections in Peru: Analí Márquez, the lawyer and leader from Cusco running alongside Roberto Sánchez}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.americatv.com.pe/noticias/actualidad/elecciones-2026-vicepresidentes-carrera-segunda-vuelta-n518337|publisher=[[América Televisión]]|language=Spanish|title=Elecciones 2026: Los vicepresidentes en carrera a segunda vuelta|trans-title=2026 Elections: Vice-presidential candidates in the running for the runoff|date=18 May 2026}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |work=National Jury of Elections (JNE) |title=Analí Márquez Huanca |url=https://votoinformado.jne.gob.pe/hoja-vida/1264/45442927/245814 |access-date=2026-06-08 }}</ref>

== Biography ==
Márquez was born on 10 October 1988, in the [[Santo Tomás District, Chumbivilcas|district of Santo Tomás]], the capital of [[Chumbivilcas province|Chumbivilcas Province]] in the [[Department of Cusco]], southern [[Peru]]. She pursued her higher education at the now-defunct [[Universidad Alas Peruanas|Alas Peruanas University]] (UAP), earning a [[Bachelor of Laws]] degree in May 2015. She later transferred to the [[Inca Garcilaso de la Vega University]] in Lima, where she qualified as a [[lawyer]] in December 2016. Subsequently, in April 2020, she enrolled in a master's program in public management at [[César Vallejo University]], graduating in August 2021.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=anali marquez huanca {{!}} Checa Bien |url=https://www.checabien.com/candidatos/presidentes/anali-marquez-huanca |access-date=2026-06-08 |website=www.checabien.com |language=es}}</ref>

=== Professional career ===
In 2018, she worked for a few months as an administrative assistant to the municipal management at the Provincial Municipality of [[Chumbivilcas province|Chumbivilcas]]. According to her official disclosures, in 2019, she served for a period in the {{Interlanguage link|Municipal Office for the Defense of Children and Adolescents|es|Defensoría del Niño y del Adolescente del Perú}} (DEMUNA) of the [[Llusco District]] Municipality. Following her entry into politics, she served as an official in the DEMUNA office at the [[Quiñota District]] Municipality between 2020 and 2021. Later, from 2023 to 2024, she was hired as a specialist in productive, environmental, and social promotion by the [[Megantoni District, La Convención province|Megantoni District]] Municipality in Cusco. Most recently, she disclosed having worked for a few months in 2025 providing legal advisory services under service contracts for the [[Lurigancho-Chosica|Lurigancho-Chosica District]] Municipality. Her tenure during this final period drew scrutiny following reports that several of the legal briefs she submitted were deficient, consisting of only a single page.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Analí Márquez Huanca |url=https://www.eleccionclara.pe/candidatos/6047 |access-date=2026-06-08 |website=Elección Clara |language=es}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Revisa Tu Candidato {{!}} Segunda Vuelta Electoral 2026: Analí Márquez Huanca |url=https://revisatucandidato.pe/?candidato=22 |access-date=2026-06-08 |website=Revisa Tu Candidato |language=es}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite news |date=2026-05-16 |title=Vicepresidenta de Roberto Sánchez cobró S/ 42 mil con informes de una sola página que solo contenían su fotografía |url=https://elcomercio.pe/politica/vicepresidenta-de-roberto-sanchez-cobro-s-42-000-con-informes-de-una-sola-pagina-que-solo-contenian-su-fotografia-viepesidenta-roberto-sanchez-anali-marquez-informes-fantasmas-municipalidad-de-chosica-oswaldo-vargas-juntos-por-el-peru-tlcnota-noticia/?ref=ecr |access-date=2026-06-08 |work=[[El Comercio (Perú)|El Comercio]] |language=es-PE |issn=1605-3052|trans-title=Roberto Sánchez's Vice Presidential Candidate Paid 42,000 PEN for Single-Page Reports Featuring Only Her Photograph|last=Cubas|first=Fiorella|url-access=subscription|location=Lima}}</ref>

== Political career ==

=== National United Renaissance ===
In the [[2020 Peruvian parliamentary election|2020 extraordinary parliamentary elections]], she ran for a seat in [[Congress of the Republic of Peru|Congress]] representing [[Department of Cusco|Cusco]] under the [[National United Resurgence|National United Renaissance]] (''Renacimiento Unido Nacional'') party. She was not elected, receiving 5,125 valid votes. In December 2021, the [[National Office of Electoral Processes]] (ONPE) initiated an administrative sanctioning procedure through Management Resolution No. RG-003014-2021-GSFP due to her failure to submit financial disclosures regarding campaign contributions, income, and expenditures from the election cycle.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |website=Jurado Nacional de Elecciones |title=Políticos: Analí Márquez Huanca |url=https://infogob.jne.gob.pe/Politico/FichaPolitico/anali-marquez-huanca_historial-partidario_9dBPe6KbLK8c6+@0ElOxMA==B6 |access-date=2026-06-08 |language=es-PE}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |work=ONPE |date=2021-12-14 |title=Resolución Gerencial N.° RG-003014-2021-GSFP |url=https://www.gob.pe/institucion/onpe/normas-legales/2548635-rg-003014-2021-gsfp |access-date=2026-06-08 |language=es-pe}}</ref>

=== Together for Peru ===
On 5 January 2022, she registered as a member of the [[Together for Peru]] (''Juntos por el Perú'') party ahead of the electoral process later that year. She subsequently ran as the party's candidate for the provincial mayoralty of [[Chumbivilcas province|Chumbivilcas]] in the [[2022 Peruvian regional and municipal elections|2022 regional and municipal elections]]. She was not elected, obtaining 1.861% of the valid votes.<ref name=":3" />

She faced public scrutiny after receiving 42,000 PEN through seven service contracts (''órdenes de servicio'') between April and October 2025 from the [[Lurigancho-Chosica|Lurigancho-Chosica District]] Municipality. The municipality was led by Mayor {{Interlanguage link|Oswaldo Vargas Cuéllar|es|Oswaldo Vargas Cuéllar}}, a fellow member of Together for Peru. The controversy centered on her legal advisory services, which were reportedly substantiated only by brief monthly reports consisting of a single page and a single photograph of herself, accompanied by short descriptions that lacked any legal analysis. In total, her contracts with this municipality amounted to 48,000 PEN. Across her career, she has accumulated 22 service contracts totaling 82,466.66 PEN, which include engagements with the municipalities of [[Quiñota District|Quiñota]], [[Llusco District|Llusco]], and Chumbivilcas.<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite web |work=Perú 21 |date=2026-05-10 |title=Elecciones 2026: Las vicepresidentas de JPP y sus polémicas propuestas |url=https://peru21.pe/investigacion/elecciones-2026-las-vicepresidentas-de-jpp-y-sus-polemicas-propuestas/ |access-date=2026-06-08 |language=es |trans-title=2026 Elections: JPP's Vice Presidential Candidates and Their Controversial Proposals}}</ref><ref name=":1" />

During the [[2026 Peruvian general election|2026 Peruvian general elections]], she was elected as a deputy representing [[Department of Cusco|Cusco]], securing a seat in the [[Chamber of Deputies (Peru)|Chamber of Deputies]] of the [[Congress of the Republic of Peru]] following the {{Interlanguage link|2026 parliamentary election in Peru|lt=April parliamentary election|es|Elecciones parlamentarias de Perú de 2026}} results. During the same electoral cycle, she ran for [[First Vice President of Peru|First Vice President]] of the nation on the presidential ticket led by [[Roberto Sánchez (Peruvian politician)|Roberto Sánchez]], which advanced to the 2026 runoff election.<ref>{{Cite web |work=Perú 21 |date=2026-04-19 |title=Elecciones 2026: Los futuros diputados y sus antecedentes |url=https://peru21.pe/investigacion/elecciones-2026-los-futuros-diputados-y-sus-antecedentes/ |access-date=2026-06-08|language=es|trans-title=2026 Elections: Future Deputies and Their Backgrounds}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-04-06 |title=Elecciones 2026: conoce a los candidatos a vicepresidentes que acompañan a Roberto Sánchez |url=https://andina.pe/agencia/noticia-elecciones-2026-conoce-a-los-candidatos-a-vicepresidentes-acompanan-a-roberto-sanchez-1069990.aspx |access-date=2026-06-08 |website=Andina|language=es|trans-title=2026 Elections: Get to Know the Vice Presidential Candidates Running Alongside Roberto Sánchez}}</ref>

=== Political positions ===
As part of her political agenda, she has expressed support for [[informal mining]], characterizing informal miners as victims of government persecution who perform a "noble and ancestral job." Her platform includes advocating for the extension of the Comprehensive Mining Formalization Registry ([[REINFO]]) and proposing modifications to the mining concession system to shorten approval periods. Additionally, she has criticized [[Multinational corporation|multinational]] formal [[List of mining companies|mining corporations]], claiming they "contribute nothing to society." She has also publicly supported the convocation of a new constituent assembly.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Espinoza |first=Analí |date=2026-04-15 |title=Experiencia y polémicas de los candidatos a la vicepresidencia de Fuerza Popular, Juntos por el Perú y Renovación Popular |url=https://www.infobae.com/peru/2026/04/15/experiencia-y-polemicas-de-los-candidatos-a-la-vicepresidencia-de-fuerza-popular-juntos-por-el-peru-y-renovacion-popular/ |access-date=2026-06-08 |website=infobae |language=es-PE|trans-title=Experience and Controversies of the Vice Presidential Candidates from Popular Force, Together for Peru, and Popular Renewal}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-04-08 |title=Los peores candidatos a vicepresidentes de las planchas que lideran las preferencias |url=https://diariocorreo.pe/politica/los-peores-candidatos-a-vicepresidentes-de-las-planchas-que-lideran-las-preferencias-noticia/ |access-date=2026-06-08 |website=Correo |language=es|author-link=Diario Correo|trans-title=The Worst Vice Presidential Candidates in the Leading Tickets}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Márquez |first=Analí |date=2026-04-06 |title=Por nuestros mineros artesanales |trans-title=For our artisanal miners |url=https://www.tiktok.com/@anali_marquez.h/video/7625868660095175943 |website=Tiktok |language=es-PE}}</ref>

'''Juan Pablo Rodríguez Oyarzún''' (born 1 November 1989) is a Chilean [[lawyer]] and [[politician]]. From March to July 2026, he served as Undersecretary of Finance under the [[presidency of José Antonio Kast]].

==Early life and education==
Rodríguez was born on 1 November 1989 in [[Viña del Mar]], Chile.<ref>{{cite web|title=Conoce quiénes asumirán como subsecretarios en el próximo gobierno de José Antonio Kast|url=https://www.emol.com/noticias/Nacional/2026/02/07/1190873/subsecretarios-gobierno-kast-gabinete-listado.html|website=Emol|date=7 February 2026|access-date=9 February 2026|language=es}}</ref> He studied law at the [[Pontifical Catholic University of Valparaíso]], where he also obtained a master's degree in law.<ref name="v">{{cite web|title=Juan Pablo Rodríguez Oyarzún|url=https://www.pucv.cl/uuaa/derecho/academicos/jornada-parcial/juan-pablo-rodriguez-oyarzun|website=Pontifical Catholic University of Valparaíso|access-date=9 February 2026|language=es}}</ref><ref name="Clinic">{{cite web|last=Munita|first=Ignacia|title=Cargo clave del equipo económico: quién es Juan Pablo Rodríguez, el abogado que es la principal carta para la Subsecretaría de Hacienda|url=https://www.theclinic.cl/2026/01/21/quien-es-juan-pablo-rodriguez-el-exasesor-de-pinera-y-cercano-a-republicanos-que-asoma-como-principal-carta-para-la-subsecretaria-de-hacienda/|website=The Clinic|date=21 January 2026|access-date=9 February 2026|language=es}}</ref>

==Professional career==
From June 2011 to June 2012, Rodríguez worked as a legislative adviser.<ref name="Clinic"/> He also served as an adviser to the [[Ministry General Secretariat of the Presidency (Chile)|Ministry General Secretariat of the Presidency]] during the first administration of President [[Sebastián Piñera]], between March 2011 and March 2014.<ref name="exante">{{cite web|title=Quiénes son los 39 subsecretarios: perfil técnico, 28 hombres y 11 mujeres y 46 años como promedio (Lea aquí la reseña de cada uno de ellos)|url=https://www.ex-ante.cl/quienes-son-los-subsecretarios-nombrados-por-kast-perfil-tecnico-28-hombres-y-11-mujeres-y-46-anos-como-promedio-lea-aqui-la-resena-de-cada-uno-de-ellos/|website=Ex-Ante|date=7 February 2026|access-date=9 February 2026|language=es}}</ref><ref name="Clinic"/>

In December 2013, he joined the think tank Fundación P!ensa, initially as a researcher and later becoming its executive director. He has taught public policy at the Department of Public Law of the Pontifical Catholic University of Valparaíso and has appeared as a panelist on the ''Nuevas Voces'' programme on [[Radio Agricultura]].<ref name="Clinic"/>

==Political career==
In 2021, Rodríguez ran as a candidate for the [[2021 Chilean Constitutional Convention election|Constitutional Convention]] in [[District 7 (Chamber of Deputies of Chile)|District 7]]. He stood as an independent candidate on a [[Independent Democratic Union]] quota within the [[Vamos por Chile]] coalition, but was not elected.<ref name="emol">{{cite web|title=Resultados Elecciones 2021 - Convención Constitucional Distrito 7|url=https://www.emol.com/especiales/2021/nacional/elecciones/resultados.asp#!c6007|website=Emol|access-date=9 February 2026|language=es}}</ref> Later that year, he ran for the [[Chamber of Deputies of Chile|Chamber of Deputies]] in the 2021 Chilean parliamentary election for the same district, but was again unsuccessful.<ref name="emol2">{{cite web|title=Resultados Elecciones 2021 - Diputados Distrito 7|url=https://www.emol.com/especiales/2021/nacional/carrera-presidencial/resultados.asp#!d6007|website=Emol|access-date=24 February 2026|language=es}}</ref>

In February 2026, president-elect [[José Antonio Kast]] announced Rodríguez's appointment as Undersecretary of Finance. He took office on 11 March 2026.<ref name="exante"/> He remained in office until 23 July 2026, when he resigned after testing positive in a drug test.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.emol.com/noticias/Economia/2026/07/23/1206542/renuncia-subsecretario-hacienda-juan-rodriguez.html|title=Renuncia el subsecretario de Hacienda Juan Pablo Rodríguez tras dar positivo a test de drogas|website=Emol|publisher=El Mercurio|date=23 July 2026|access-date=24 July 2026|language=es}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://puranoticia.pnt.cl/nacional/presidente-kast-acepto-la-renuncia-de-juan-pablo-rodriguez-al-cargo-de|title=Presidente Kast aceptó la renuncia de Juan Pablo Rodríguez al cargo de subsecretario de Hacienda|website=Puranoticia|access-date=24 July 2026|language=es}}</ref>

{{short description|Mexican politician (born 1986)}}
[[File:Ruth González de Gallardo.jpg|thumb|González Silva in 2019]]
'''Ruth Miriam González Silva de Gallardo'''{{efn|In this [[Mexican name]], the first or paternal surname is ''[[González (surname)|González]]'',  the second or maternal surname is ''[[Silva]]'' and, for married women, the optional marital name is ''de [[Gallardo]]''.}} (born 6 August 1986) is a Mexican politician affiliated with the [[Ecologist Green Party of Mexico]] (PVEM). She was elected to the [[Senate (Mexico)|Senate]] for the state of [[San Luis Potosí]] in the [[2024 Mexican Senate election|2024 general election]] and has been announced as her party's prospective candidate for the [[governor of San Luis Potosí|governorship of San Luis Potosí]] in the [[2027 Mexican local elections|2027 election]].

==Political career==
Ruth González Silva was born in [[San Luis Potosí, San Luis Potosí]], in 1986. She holds a bachelor's degree in communication science.<ref name=sil66>{{cite web |title=Perfil: Sen. Ruth Miriam González Silva, LXVI Legislatura |publisher=[[Secretariat of the Interior|SEGOB]] |website=Sistema de Información Legislativa (SIL) |access-date=28 September 2026 |url=https://sil.gobernacion.gob.mx/Librerias/pp_PerfilLegislador.php?Referencia=9229092}}</ref>

She ran unsuccessfully for the Senate in the [[2018 Mexican general election|2018 election]] on the [[Party of the Democratic Revolution]] (PRD) ticket<ref name=sil66/> but, in the 2024 general election, representing the PVEM, she was elected to [[San Luis Potosí]]'s first Senate seat for the [[LXVI Legislature of the Mexican Congress|2024–2030 term]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Senadurías: San Luis Potosí |url=https://computos2024.ine.mx/senadurias/nacional/entidad/24/candidatura |website=Cómputos Distritales 2024 |publisher=[[National Electoral Institute|INE]] |access-date=28 September 2026}}</ref>

On 13 July 2026, [[Ricardo Gallardo]], the incumbent [[governor of San Luis Potosí]], announced her as the PVEM's candidate to succeed him in the [[2027 Mexican local elections|gubernatorial election]] of 6 June 2027.<ref name=destape>{{cite news |title=Ricardo Gallardo 'destapa' a su esposa para la gubernatura de SLP |url=https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/estados/2026/07/13/ricardo-gallardo-destapa-a-su-esposa-para-la-gubernatura-de-slp-les-presento-a-una-gran-mujer/ |work=[[El Financiero]] |date=13 July  2026}}</ref> Gallardo is González's husband, but he refuted claims that her nomination was an act of [[nepotism]] and argued 
that the recently adopted constitutional amendment prohibiting family members of current officeholders from seeking the same elected position is not scheduled to take effect until 2030.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Diego |first1=Anaid |title=Gobernador de SLP 'destapa' a su esposa para sucederlo en 2027 |url=https://mvsnoticias.com/nacional/estados/2026/7/14/gobernador-de-slp-destapa-su-esposa-para-sucederlo-en-2027-738402.html |work=[[MVS Noticias]] |date=14 July 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Aguilar Esquivel |first1=Israel |title=Diputados aprueban reforma contra nepotismo electoral y no reelección; aplicará en 2030 |url=https://www.infobae.com/mexico/2025/03/04/diputados-aprueban-en-lo-general-reforma-contra-nepotismo-electoral-y-no-reeleccion-discuten-si-aplicara-en-2027-o-2030/ |work=[[Infobae]] |date=4 March 2025}}</ref>

==Personal life==
González Silva is married to [[Ricardo Gallardo]], who was elected to a six-year term as [[governor of San Luis Potosí]] in 2021.<ref name=destape/> They have two children.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Sustaita |first1=Sharon |title=¿Quién es Ruth González Silva? Senadora por San Luis Potosí |url=https://www.sdpnoticias.com/estados/quien-es-ruth-gonzalez-silva-senadora-por-san-luis-potosi-protagonizo-debate-por-reforma-contra-el-nepotismo/ |work=SDP Noticias |date=26 February 2025}}</ref>
